WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.TITLE: What is Rideshare Insurance and Why Do You Need It?
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC1: Rideshare driving comes with unique risks that standard personal auto policies often don’t fully cover. When you switch on a rideshare app and start accepting passengers, your coverage situation changes instantly. This is where rideshare insurance becomes important. It helps fill the gaps between your personal policy and the limited coverage offered by rideshare companies, ensuring you’re not left exposed while driving.
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC2: Without proper coverage, drivers can face serious financial setbacks after an accident, especially during waiting periods or in-between-ride phases. A rideshare policy is designed to protect you, your vehicle, and your passengers at every stage of your trip. With the right guidance, you can find coverage that keeps you fully protected while staying compliant with insurance requirements.
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.SUB_TITLE: Rideshare insurance is essential for several reasons, including:

LIST.TITLE: Coverage Gap Protection
LIST.TEXT: Fills critical gaps between your personal auto policy and the limited coverage provided by rideshare companies, especially during app-on waiting periods when drivers are most vulnerable to uncovered risks and unexpected expenses.

LIST.TITLE: Financial Security
LIST.TEXT: Protects you from high out-of-pocket costs after accidents, vehicle damage, or liability claims, helping you avoid financial strain while continuing your rideshare work with confidence and better long-term stability.

LIST.TITLE: Driver Compliance
LIST.TEXT: Keeps you aligned insurance regulations and rideshare platform requirements, ensuring you are legally covered while driving and avoiding penalties, policy cancellations, or complications that could disrupt your ability to earn.

LIST.TITLE: Vehicle Protection
LIST.TEXT: Extends coverage to your car during periods where personal policies fall short, helping cover repairs or damages so your vehicle stays protected, reliable, and ready for daily rideshare use without unnecessary risk.

LIST.TITLE: Peace of Mind
LIST.TEXT: Gives you confidence on every trip by ensuring you have the right protection in place, allowing you to focus on passengers, safety, and earnings without constantly worrying about coverage gaps or unexpected issues.

AUTO_COVERAGE.TITLE: Does My Personal Auto Insurance Cover Me While Driving for Uber or Lyft?
AUTO_COVERAGE.DESC1: Most personal auto insurance policies are not designed to cover rideshare activity. The moment you turn on a rideshare app like Uber or Lyft, your vehicle is no longer considered for personal use only. This creates a gap in coverage, especially while you are waiting for ride requests. That’s why many drivers look for auto insurance for rideshare drivers to avoid unexpected risks
AUTO_COVERAGE.DESC2: Rideshare companies do provide limited coverage, but it often only applies during specific phases of a trip. If an accident happens outside those active periods, you could be left paying out of pocket. Having the right coverage in place ensures you stay protected at all times, without confusion about when your policy applies.

COVERAGE_GAP.TITLE: What is the Coverage Gap in Rideshare Insurance?
COVERAGE_GAP.DESC1: The coverage gap in rideshare insurance refers to the period when your personal auto policy no longer applies, but the rideshare company’s insurance has not fully taken over. This usually happens when the app is turned on, and you are waiting for a ride request. During this time, your risk increases, yet your protection may be limited or incomplete.
COVERAGE_GAP.DESC2: The coverage gap in rideshare insurance refers to the period when your personal auto policy no longer applies, but the rideshare company’s insurance has not fully taken over. If an accident occurs in this phase, drivers often discover their personal policy may deny the claim, while the rideshare company’s coverage may not fully cover damages or liability. This gap can lead to unexpected expenses and financial stress. Having the right rideshare coverage helps bridge this gap, ensuring continuous protection from the moment you go online until your last ride is completed.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Rideshare Insurance Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Rideshare insurance in Texas provides added protection beyond standard policies by covering key risk areas drivers face daily. It can include liability for injuries or property damage, repair costs for your vehicle, and protection during app-on periods. Coverage often extends to uninsured drivers and certain medical expenses, helping reduce financial stress and keeping your work on track.

LIST.TITLE: Bodily Injury Liability
LIST.DESC: Protects you if a passenger, other driver, or pedestrian is injured in an accident you cause. Covers medical bills, lost wages, and legal costs, ensuring financial security while driving for rideshare platforms like Uber or Lyft.

LIST.TITLE: Property Damage Liability
LIST.DESC: Covers damage your vehicle causes to someone else's property, including vehicles, buildings, or fences. Ensures you don't pay out-of-pocket for repairs or replacements while driving passengers or delivering goods through rideshare apps.

LIST.TITLE: Collision Coverage
LIST.DESC: Pays for repairs to your vehicle after an accident, regardless of who's at fault. Helps keep your car roadworthy without financial stress and ensures you can continue driving for rideshare without interruptions or large repair bills.

LIST.TITLE: Comprehensive Coverage
LIST.DESC: Protects against non-collision events like theft, fire, vandalism, or natural disasters. Ensures your vehicle is repaired or replaced without financial burden, giving you peace of mind while working as a rideshare driver.

LIST.TITLE: Uninsured / Underinsured Motorist Coverage
LIST.DESC: Covers damages and medical expenses if you're hit by a driver with insufficient or no insurance. Protects your finances and ensures you and your passengers have support in the event of an accident involving an underinsured or uninsured motorist.

LIST.TITLE: Medical Payments & Personal Injury Protection
LIST.DESC: Helps pay medical bills for you and your passengers after an accident, regardless of fault. Covers emergency care, hospital costs, and rehabilitation, ensuring you can focus on recovery without worrying about financial strain.

LIST.TITLE: Period 1 Coverage Gap Protection (App On — No Passenger)
LIST.DESC: Period 1 coverage gap protects you during the app-on waiting period before a ride is accepted. Fills the gap between personal and company coverage, keeping you financially secure from accidents or damages during downtime between passengers.

LIST.TITLE: Period 2 Coverage (Ride Accepted — En Route to Passenger)
LIST.DESC: Period 2 coverage plan covers you once a ride is accepted and you're driving to pick up a passenger. Provides liability and damage protection during this active phase, ensuring you're not exposed to financial risk while performing rideshare duties.

LIST.TITLE: Period 3 Coverage (Passenger In Vehicle)
LIST.DESC: Covers you while passengers are in your vehicle, including liability, collision, and medical costs. Protects both drivers and riders during trips, ensuring you meet the safety and financial responsibilities required by rideshare platforms.

LIST.TITLE: Passenger Injury Coverage
LIST.DESC: Provides medical and legal coverage if a passenger is injured while riding with you. Ensures protection for you as the driver, maintains compliance with insurance requirements, and keeps your rideshare work safe and secure.

LIST.TITLE: Delivery Coverage (Food & Grocery Platforms)
LIST.DESC: Extends protection for deliveries of food, groceries, or packages via platforms such as Uber Eats, DoorDash, or Postmates. Covers liability and vehicle damage, giving drivers confidence to safely complete deliveries without financial worry.

LIST.TITLE: Rental Reimbursement During Repairs
LIST.DESC: Covers rental vehicle expenses while your car is being repaired after an accident or damage. Ensures you can continue your rideshare work without interruption, maintaining your income and minimizing downtime due to vehicle repairs.

LIST.TITLE: Roadside Assistance & Towing
LIST.DESC: Provides help when your vehicle breaks down, including towing, battery jump-starts, tire changes, or fuel delivery. Ensures you can get back on the road quickly, reducing lost income and inconvenience during rideshare operations.

LIST.TITLE: Gap Insurance for Financed Vehicles
LIST.DESC: Covers the difference between your car's current market value and what you owe on a loan or lease if your vehicle is totaled. Prevents financial loss for drivers with financed or leased cars, keeping rideshare work sustainable.

LIST.TITLE: Multi-Platform Coverage (Uber & Lyft Simultaneously)
LIST.DESC: Allows coverage while driving for multiple rideshare platforms simultaneously. Ensures you remain protected whether you accept trips on Uber, Lyft, or other apps, providing seamless financial security for all rideshare activity.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Rideshare Insurance NOT Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Rideshare insurance in Texas does not cover intentional damage, personal belongings inside your vehicle, or accidents that happen while driving for non-approved purposes. It also may exclude coverage for unauthorized drivers, high-risk modifications, or incidents caused by impaired driving. Knowing these limitations helps drivers avoid gaps and stay fully protected.

PERSONAL_USE_ACCIDENTS.TITLE: Personal Use Accidents on a Commercial-Only Policy
PERSONAL_USE_ACCIDENTS.DESC: Accidents that happen while driving for personal reasons on a commercial-only rideshare policy are not covered. This means insurance applies only to approved rideshare activities, leaving drivers responsible for costs incurred during personal trips.

INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE.TITLE: Intentional Damage or Fraud
INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE.DESC: Rideshare insurance will not pay for damages caused intentionally or through fraudulent actions. Any claims from deliberate harm to your vehicle or false reporting can be denied, protecting insurers from abuse and drivers from policy misuse.

WEAR_TEAR.TITLE: Normal Wear & Tear & Mechanical Breakdown
WEAR_TEAR.DESC: Regular wear, mechanical failures, or maintenance issues are not covered. Rideshare insurance focuses on accident and liability protection, not routine repairs or replacement of worn parts, ensuring coverage only applies to covered incidents.

DUI.TITLE: Driving Under the Influence
DUI.DESC: Any accident occurring while driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs is excluded. Policies will not cover damages or liability resulting from impaired driving, emphasizing the safe and legal operation of your vehicle at all times.

UNLISTED_DRIVERS.TITLE: Unlisted Drivers Operating Your Vehicle
UNLISTED_DRIVERS.DESC: Unlisted drivers operating your vehicle insurance does not cover accidents caused by drivers not listed on your policy. If an unapproved person uses your vehicle, any damages or liability arising from their actions will fall on you personally.

PASSENGER_INJURIES_BEYOND_LIMITS.TITLE: Passengers Injured Beyond Platform Coverage Limits
PASSENGER_INJURIES_BEYOND_LIMITS.DESC: If a passenger is injured and their medical expenses exceed the platform or policy limits, rideshare insurance may not cover the remaining costs. Drivers are responsible for ensuring coverage fits potential passenger risks.

PERSONAL_BELONGINGS.TITLE: Personal Belongings & Property Inside the Vehicle
PERSONAL_BELONGINGS.DESC: Items inside your car, such as bags, electronics, or personal property, are not covered. Insurance protects the vehicle and passengers, but personal belongings lost or damaged during rideshare trips are the driver's responsibility.

RACING_RECKLESS.TITLE: Racing & Reckless Driving
RACING_RECKLESS.DESC: Any accidents resulting from racing, aggressive maneuvers, or reckless driving are excluded. Racing driver policies protect only drivers operating safely and legally, encouraging responsible behavior while earning through rideshare apps.

NO_VALID_LICENSE.TITLE: Driving Without a Valid License
NO_VALID_LICENSE.DESC: If an accident occurs while operating a vehicle without a valid driver's license, insurance will not cover damages. Maintaining a valid license is essential for both legal compliance and eligibility for rideshare insurance coverage.

UNAPPROVED_VEHICLES.TITLE: Vehicles Not Approved by the Rideshare Platform
UNAPPROVED_VEHICLES.DESC: Vehicles that do not meet platform requirements or are unapproved are not covered. Using an unlisted vehicle or one not approved by the rideshare platform voids coverage, leaving the driver financially liable for accidents or damages.

COMMERCIAL_DELIVERY.TITLE: Commercial Delivery Without Proper Endorsement
COMMERCIAL_DELIVERY.DESC: Deliveries made without the proper insurance endorsement or coverage are excluded. Drivers must ensure policies include delivery activities, such as grocery services, to avoid gaps in the protection of commercial delivery without proper endorsement.

UNAUTHORIZED_PLATFORM_USE.TITLE: Accidents During Unauthorized Platform Use
UNAUTHORIZED_PLATFORM_USE.DESC: Accidents that occur while using a rideshare app for unauthorized purposes, such as personal errands or unapproved services, are not covered. Insurance only applies during officially sanctioned rideshare operations.

GAP_COVERAGE.TITLE: Gap Between Vehicle Value & Loan Balance (Without Gap Coverage)
GAP_COVERAGE.DESC: If your vehicle is totaled or severely damaged, and your loan or lease balance exceeds the car's actual market value, the difference will not be covered without gap insurance. Drivers are responsible for paying the remaining balance out of pocket.

MEXICO_DRIVING.TITLE: Driving in Mexico Without Mexican Insurance
MEXICO_DRIVING.DESC: Rideshare insurance does not extend into Mexico. If an accident occurs while driving there without proper Mexican insurance, you are fully liable for damages, medical bills, and legal costs. Additional coverage is required to stay protected.

WAR_NUCLEAR.TITLE: War & Nuclear Exclusions
WAR_NUCLEAR.DESC: Rideshare insurance policies do not cover damages or liability resulting from war, acts of terrorism, or nuclear incidents. Any catastrophic events outside normal driving risks are excluded, leaving drivers responsible for losses.

DRIVING_PERIODS.TITLE: Understanding the 3 Rideshare Driving Periods — and What Each Covers
DRIVING_PERIODS.INTRO: Rideshare driving in Texas is divided into three main periods, each with different coverage rules that determine how and when insurance applies.

LIST.TITLE: Period 1 (App On — No Ride Accepted)
LIST.DESC: Period 1 begins when you turn on your rideshare app but have not yet accepted a ride. During this time, personal auto policies often do not apply, and rideshare company coverage is limited. Proper rideshare insurance fills this gap, keeping you protected while waiting for ride requests and preventing unexpected out-of-pocket costs.

LIST.TITLE: Period 2 (Ride Accepted — En Route to Passenger)
LIST.DESC: Period 2 starts once you accept a ride and are driving to pick up your passenger. Liability coverage is generally active during this phase, protecting you against claims for bodily injury or property damage. Some policies may also include collision and comprehensive coverage, ensuring financial protection if an accident occurs while en route.

LIST.TITLE: Period 3 (Passenger In Vehicle)
LIST.DESC: Period 3 covers the time when your passenger is in the vehicle. Full liability protection, collision coverage, and passenger injury protection typically apply during this phase. This is the highest-risk period, making comprehensive rideshare insurance essential to protect both you and your passengers.

WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.TITLE: What is Renters Insurance and Why Do You Need It?
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC: Renters' insurance is a type of home insurance policy designed to protect tenants' personal property and belongings from unexpected incidents such as theft, fire, or damage. It also provides liability coverage in case someone is injured in your rental space or if you cause damage to someone else's property. While your landlord’s insurance covers the building itself, renters' insurance protects your personal items.
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.SUB_TITLE: Here are the most important reasons renters insurance is essential:

LIST.TITLE: Protection for Personal Property
LIST.TEXT: Renters insurance covers the cost of replacing or repairing personal belongings, such as furniture, electronics, clothes, and appliances, in case they are damaged or stolen. Without it, you could be left to pay for these expenses out of pocket.

LIST.TITLE: Liability Coverage
LIST.TEXT: If someone is injured in your rented space, renters' insurance can help cover medical expenses and legal fees if you're found liable. It can protect you from costly lawsuits related to accidents on your property.

LIST.TITLE: Affordable Coverage
LIST.TEXT: Renters insurance is relatively inexpensive, often costing as little as $15-$20 per month. This is a small price to pay for peace of mind knowing that your personal items and liability are covered.

LIST.TITLE: Additional Living Expenses
LIST.TEXT: If your rental becomes uninhabitable due to damage from a covered event (like a fire), renters insurance can help cover additional living expenses, such as hotel bills, until your home is repaired.

LIST.TITLE: Protection Against Theft and Vandalism
LIST.TEXT: Renters insurance provides coverage for stolen or vandalized property, both inside your rental unit and even for belongings stored outside (like in a car). This helps safeguard your valuables from unexpected loss.

RENTERS_REQUIRED.TITLE: Is Renters Insurance Required in Texas?
RENTERS_REQUIRED.DESC1: Renters' insurance is not legally required in Texas. However, many landlords and property management companies make it a mandatory condition for leasing their property. This requirement is designed to protect both the tenant and the landlord in the event of accidents, damage, or other unforeseen events. While the law doesn't mandate renters' insurance, it is a common stipulation in rental agreements.
RENTERS_REQUIRED.DESC2: Even though renters insurance isn't required by the state, it's still a smart decision to have coverage. It can protect your personal belongings, cover liability costs, and help with additional living expenses in the event of an emergency, such as a fire or water damage. Without renters insurance, you could face a significant financial burden in the event of a disaster or accident.

LANDLOAD_INSURANCE.TITLE: Does My Landlord's Insurance Cover My Belongings?
LANDLOAD_INSURANCE.DESC1: No, your landlord's insurance does not cover your personal belongings. Landlord insurance typically covers the building's structure, including common areas, and any damage to the property caused by events such as fire or weather. However, it does not extend to the tenant's possessions inside the rental unit. If your personal items are damaged, stolen, or destroyed, you would be responsible for replacing them unless you have renters' insurance.
LANDLOAD_INSURANCE.DESC2: To ensure your belongings are protected, it’s essential to have renters' insurance. This policy will cover the cost of replacing or repairing your personal property in the event of theft, fire, or water damage. Without it, you would bear the full financial responsibility for any loss or damage to your possessions.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Renters Insurance Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Renters insurance provides financial protection for tenants by covering personal belongings, liability risks, and additional living expenses. It protects against common risks such as theft, fire, vandalism, and certain natural disasters. Optional add-ons and endorsements can further enhance your coverage based on your lifestyle and valuable possessions.

STANDARD.TITLE: Standard Coverages (Included in Most Policies)
STANDARD.DESC: Most renters insurance policies include essential protections that cover personal belongings, liability risks, and temporary living expenses. These coverages ensure tenants are protected from unexpected financial losses.

LIST.TITLE: Personal Belongings & Contents
LIST.DESC: Renters insurance covers the cost of replacing personal items like clothing, furniture, and electronics if they are damaged, stolen, or destroyed. This ensures that you're not left financially burdened when an unexpected event occurs.

LIST.TITLE: Furniture & Appliances
LIST.DESC: Your renters' insurance policy helps cover the replacement costs of furniture and appliances damaged by fire, smoke, or other events. Whether it's a sofa, refrigerator, or washing machine, your belongings will be protected under your policy's limits.

LIST.TITLE: Electronics & Technology
LIST.DESC: Electronics such as phones, laptops, and TVs are covered by renters' insurance if they are lost, stolen, or damaged due to a covered event. This ensures you don't have to pay out of pocket to replace devices after incidents.

LIST.TITLE: Clothing & Accessories
LIST.DESC: Renters insurance covers your clothing and accessories in the event of theft, fire, or other damage. Whether it's a favorite jacket or expensive shoes, your personal wardrobe is protected under the terms of your renters' insurance policy.

LIST.TITLE: Jewelry & Valuables (Up to Policy Limits)
LIST.DESC: High-value items like jewelry, art, or collectibles are typically covered by renters insurance, up to a certain limit. If you have valuable items, it's a good idea to schedule them for higher coverage to ensure they are fully protected against loss or damage.

LIST.TITLE: Liability Coverage for Bodily Injury
LIST.DESC: Liability coverage in renters insurance helps protect you if someone is injured while on your property. Whether it's a slip-and-fall or another accident, this coverage helps pay for medical expenses and legal fees if you are held responsible.

LIST.TITLE: Liability Coverage for Property Damage
LIST.DESC: This aspect of renters insurance covers the cost of damage you might cause to someone else's property, either by accident or negligence. Whether it's breaking a neighbor's window or damaging someone's furniture, this coverage helps pay for repairs.

LIST.TITLE: Additional Living Expenses & Loss of Use
LIST.DESC: If your rental unit becomes uninhabitable due to a covered event, renters' insurance will help cover additional living expenses, such as hotel stays or temporary rentals, until the home is repaired. This ensures you aren't left without a place to stay.

LIST.TITLE: Medical Payments to Others
LIST.DESC: This coverage helps pay for medical expenses if someone is injured on your property, regardless of who is at fault. Whether it's a guest or a visitor, this part of renters insurance can cover their medical bills for minor injuries sustained.

LIST.TITLE: Fire & Smoke Damage
LIST.DESC: Fire and smoke damage is typically covered under renters' insurance, helping you replace personal property damaged or destroyed in a fire. The policy may also cover cleanup and repair costs, ensuring you aren't financially responsible for the damage.

LIST.TITLE: Theft & Burglary
LIST.DESC: Renters insurance protects against theft or burglary by covering the cost to replace stolen personal property. If someone breaks into your home and takes your electronics or furniture, your policy can help recover the financial loss up to your coverage limit.

LIST.TITLE: Vandalism & Malicious Mischief
LIST.DESC: If your property is damaged by vandalism or other malicious acts, renters' insurance helps cover repair or replacement costs. This includes damage from graffiti, broken windows, or other deliberate acts intended to harm your belongings.

LIST.TITLE: Water Damage (Sudden & Accidental)
LIST.DESC: Water damage from sudden and accidental incidents, such as burst pipes or leaks, is typically covered by renters' insurance. This coverage can help with repairs and the replacement of belongings damaged by water, ensuring you're not left facing financial hardship after an incident.

LIST.TITLE: Wind & Hail Damage
LIST.DESC: Damage from windstorms or hail is covered by renters' insurance, as long as the damage is not the result of negligence. Whether it's damage to your personal belongings or the structure of the rental itself, your policy can help cover repair and replacement costs.

LIST.TITLE: Belongings Stored Outside the Apartment
LIST.DESC: Many renters' insurance policies cover personal belongings stored outside your apartment, such as in a storage unit or garage. If your items are stolen or damaged while in these areas, your insurance will help cover the cost of replacements.

LIST.TITLE: Belongings in Your Car (Up to Policy Limits)
LIST.DESC: Renters insurance may cover personal belongings inside your car, such as a laptop or a camera, if they're stolen or damaged. However, the coverage is subject to the policy's limits, so it's essential to review your policy for specific conditions.

LIST.TITLE: Identity Theft Protection (With Endorsement)
LIST.DESC: Renters insurance with an identity theft endorsement can help protect against identity fraud. This coverage may include assistance with restoring your identity and covering expenses such as legal fees or lost wages resulting from identity theft.

LIST.TITLE: Scheduled Personal Property (High-Value Items)
LIST.DESC: If you have high-value items like fine art, expensive jewelry, or collectibles, renters insurance can provide additional coverage through a scheduled personal property endorsement. This adds extra protection for these items.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Renters Insurance NOT Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: While renters insurance provides broad protection for personal belongings and liability, there are important exclusions to understand. Standard policies do not cover certain natural disasters, structural damage, or specific types of losses unless additional coverage or endorsements are added. Knowing these exclusions helps you avoid surprises and ensures you have the right protection.

FLOOD_DAMAGE.TITLE: Flood Damage
FLOOD_DAMAGE.DESC: Standard renters insurance does not cover damage caused by flooding due to heavy rain, storms, or rising water. A separate flood insurance policy is required.

EARTHQUAKE_DAMAGE.TITLE: Earthquake Damage
EARTHQUAKE_DAMAGE.DESC: Damage from earthquakes is not included in standard renters insurance. Separate earthquake coverage is needed for protection.

STRUCTURAL_DAMAGE.TITLE: Structural Damage to the Building
STRUCTURAL_DAMAGE.DESC: Renters insurance does not cover damage to the building structure. This is the landlord’s responsibility under their property insurance.

ROOMMATE_BELONGINGS.TITLE: Roommate's Belongings
ROOMMATE_BELONGINGS.DESC: Your policy does not cover your roommate’s belongings unless they are specifically added or endorsed. Each tenant typically needs their own policy.

HIGH_VALUE_LIMITS.TITLE: High-Value Items Beyond Limits
HIGH_VALUE_LIMITS.DESC: Expensive items like jewelry, art, or collectibles may only be covered up to a sublimit unless scheduled separately for higher coverage.

PEST_DAMAGE.TITLE: Pest & Bed Bug Damage
PEST_DAMAGE.DESC: Damage caused by pests, insects, or bed bugs is not covered, as it is considered preventable through maintenance.

MOLD_MILDEW.TITLE: Mold & Mildew Damage
MOLD_MILDEW.DESC: Mold damage is generally not covered unless it results directly from a covered event like a burst pipe.

WEAR_TEAR.TITLE: Normal Wear & Tear
WEAR_TEAR.DESC: Gradual damage from everyday use, aging, or lack of maintenance is not covered by renters insurance.

BUSINESS_PROPERTY.TITLE: Business Equipment & Inventory
BUSINESS_PROPERTY.DESC: Business-related property is not covered unless you add a specific endorsement or separate business insurance.

VEHICLE_DAMAGE.TITLE: Vehicle Damage
VEHICLE_DAMAGE.DESC: Damage to your vehicle is not covered by renters' insurance, as this is handled by your auto insurance policy. If your car is damaged or stolen, you'll need to file a claim with your car insurance provider, not your renters insurance.

INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE.TITLE: Intentional Damage or Fraud
INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE.DESC: Any damage caused intentionally or through fraudulent claims is excluded from coverage.

POWER_OUTAGE.TITLE: Power Outage & Food Spoilage
POWER_OUTAGE.DESC: Losses from power outages, such as spoiled food, are not covered unless you add an endorsement.

SEWER_BACKUP.TITLE: Sewer & Drain Backup
SEWER_BACKUP.DESC: Damage from sewer or drain backups is typically excluded unless additional coverage is purchased.

WAR_NUCLEAR.TITLE: War & Nuclear Events
WAR_NUCLEAR.DESC: Losses caused by war, terrorism, or nuclear hazards are excluded from standard renters insurance policies.

POLICY_LIMITS.TITLE: Losses Beyond Policy Limits
POLICY_LIMITS.DESC: Renters insurance only pays up to your coverage limits. Any losses exceeding those limits must be paid out of pocket.

WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.TITLE: What is Condo Insurance and Why Do You Need It?
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC: Condo insurance is a specialized insurance policy for condominium owners that protects their personal belongings, interior space, and liability. While your building’s master policy covers common areas and the exterior, your condo insurance safeguards the parts you are responsible for, from walls and flooring to appliances and furniture. It ensures that unexpected events like fire, theft, or water damage don’t leave you facing costly repairs or out-of-pocket replacements.
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC1: Beyond protecting property, condo insurance provides financial security if someone is injured inside your unit. Liability coverage helps cover medical bills, legal fees, or damages, giving you peace of mind. Many policies also cover additional living expenses if your condo becomes temporarily uninhabitable, so you can maintain your lifestyle while repairs are made. Choosing the right policy is essential, and a broker can help you find the best coverage, including affordable condo insurance, tailored to your needs.

LIST.TITLE: Understanding Condo Insurance
LIST.TEXT: Condo insurance is a policy designed specifically for condominium owners, covering your personal belongings, interior structure, and liability. Unlike homeowners' insurance, it complements the building’s master policy, protecting areas you’re responsible for inside your unit.

LIST.TITLE: Protection for Personal Property
LIST.TEXT: Your furniture, electronics, clothing, and other valuables are vulnerable to theft, fire, or damage. Condo insurance ensures you can replace or repair these items without a major financial setback.

LIST.TITLE: Liability Coverage Matters
LIST.TEXT: Accidents can happen inside your condo. If someone is injured or property is damaged, liability coverage helps cover medical costs or legal fees, keeping you financially secure.

LIST.TITLE: Additional Living Expenses
LIST.TEXT: If your condo becomes temporarily uninhabitable due to a covered event, your insurance may cover hotel stays, meals, and other necessary living expenses until repairs are complete.

LIST.TITLE: Choosing the Right Policy
LIST.TEXT: Finding the right coverage tailored to your needs is essential. A trusted broker can help compare plans and provide affordable condo insurance that fits your lifestyle and budget.

CONDO_REQUIRED.TITLE: Is Condo Insurance Required in Texas?
CONDO_REQUIRED.DESC1: In Texas, condo insurance is not legally required, but it is often mandated by your mortgage lender. If you are financing your condominium, lenders typically require coverage to protect their investment in case of damage, fire, or other covered events. Even if you own your condo outright, having insurance is a smart safeguard against unexpected costs, such as theft, water damage, or liability claims from visitors.
CONDO_REQUIRED.DESC2: Additionally, your condo association's master policy usually covers common areas and the building structure, but it does not protect your personal belongings or the interior of your unit. Without condo insurance, you would be responsible for these repairs and replacements yourself. Liability coverage is also critical, as it protects you from legal or medical costs if someone is injured inside your condo. In short, while not always legally required, condo insurance is highly recommended to ensure financial security and peace of mind.

POLICY_COVER.TITLE: Does My HOA's Master Policy Cover My Unit?
POLICY_COVER.DESC1: Your HOA's master policy primarily protects the common areas and exterior structure of the condominium, such as the roof, building walls, hallways, and shared amenities. While this coverage is important, it typically does not extend to the interior of your unit or your personal belongings. Items like furniture, electronics, appliances, and personal decor are usually your responsibility, so any damage or loss to these items is not covered by the HOA policy.
POLICY_COVER.DESC2: Liability protection is another area where the master policy may fall short. If someone is injured inside your unit or you accidentally cause damage to a neighbor's property, your personal liability coverage through a condo insurance policy is essential. Without it, you could face high out-of-pocket costs. For comprehensive protection, pairing your HOA's master policy with a personalized condo insurance plan ensures both your unit and belongings are fully safeguarded.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Condo Insurance Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Condo insurance in Texas protects your personal belongings, interior structure, and liability. It covers furniture, electronics, appliances, and clothing from fire, theft, or water damage. Liability protection handles injuries or property damage inside your unit. Many policies also include additional living expenses if your condo is temporarily uninhabitable due to a covered event.

STANDARD.TITLE: Standard Coverages (Included in Most Policies)
STANDARD.DESC: Most condo insurance policies include essential protections that cover personal property, interior structure, liability risks, and temporary living expenses. These coverages ensure condo owners are protected from unexpected financial losses.

LIST.TITLE: Personal Property
LIST.DESC: Condo insurance protects your personal items, such as furniture, electronics, clothing, and other valuables. It covers theft, fire, water damage, or other covered events, ensuring you can replace or repair belongings without paying out of pocket.

LIST.TITLE: Interior Structure (Walls-In Coverage)
LIST.DESC: Covers the interior of your condo, including walls, floors, ceilings, cabinets, and built-in appliances. Complements the HOA master policy by protecting areas inside your unit, so repairs or replacements don't cost you money after covered events.

LIST.TITLE: Personal Liability
LIST.DESC: Protects you if someone is injured inside your condo or you accidentally damage another person's property. Covers medical bills, legal fees, or settlements, keeping you financially secure against claims or lawsuits that may arise from accidents.

LIST.TITLE: Loss of Use / Additional Living Expenses
LIST.DESC: Pays for hotel stays, meals, and living costs if your condo becomes uninhabitable due to a covered event. Ensures your lifestyle continues while repairs are completed, helping you avoid financial stress during temporary displacement.

LIST.TITLE: Loss Assessment Coverage
LIST.DESC: Covers special assessments by your HOA due to damage in shared areas. Protects you from unexpected costs if the association needs extra funds for repairs, ensuring your portion is covered, and your finances remain protected.

LIST.TITLE: Medical Payments to Others
LIST.DESC: Pays for minor medical expenses if a guest is injured in your condo, regardless of fault. It covers treatment costs or small claims without the need to file a formal liability claim, providing quick and efficient resolution for accidents.

LIST.TITLE: Water Backup and Sump Pump Overflow
LIST.DESC: Protects your condo from damage caused by water backup, sewer clogs, or sump pump failure. This coverage ensures floors, walls, and personal property are repaired or replaced without financial burden, protecting against costly water damage.

LIST.TITLE: Improvements and Betterments (Upgrades & Renovations)
LIST.DESC: Covers upgrades, renovations, or improvements made to your unit, including new flooring, cabinets, or built-in appliances. It ensures your investments are protected and can be restored if damaged by fire, water, theft, or other covered causes.

LIST.TITLE: Jewelry, Art & High-Value Items
LIST.DESC: Provides extra protection for high-value items such as jewelry, artwork, and collectibles. Standard condo insurance may limit coverage, so this ensures you can repair or replace valuable possessions without facing financial hardship.

LIST.TITLE: Electronics and Appliances
LIST.DESC: Covers computers, TVs, kitchen appliances, and other essential electronics from theft, fire, or water damage. This ensures you can replace or repair devices without extra cost, maintaining the convenience and functionality of your condo.

LIST.TITLE: Clothing and Furniture
LIST.DESC: Protects clothing, bedding, sofas, tables, and other personal furnishings from loss due to fire, theft, water damage, or vandalism. This coverage ensures you can restore or replace items in your home without a significant financial impact.

LIST.TITLE: Guest Medical Protection
LIST.DESC: Pays for minor injuries that guests sustain while visiting your condo, covering medical expenses regardless of fault. This ensures small accidents are handled quickly and efficiently, preventing potential liability claims or out-of-pocket costs.

LIST.TITLE: Identity Theft Coverage
LIST.DESC: Helps cover expenses related to identity theft, including legal fees, credit monitoring, and lost funds. If your personal information is stolen, this coverage helps you recover, restore your financial identity, and mitigate stress.

LIST.TITLE: Refrigerated Property Coverage
LIST.DESC: Protects food, medications, and other refrigerated items from spoilage caused by power outages, equipment failures, or accidental loss. This coverage ensures essential items remain protected and reduces financial losses from perishable property.

LIST.TITLE: Fire and Smoke Damage
LIST.DESC: Covers damage caused by fire or smoke inside your condo. This includes property, interior structure, and cleanup costs. With this coverage, repairs and replacements are managed without significant financial strain, ensuring your home is restored.

LIST.TITLE: Theft and Vandalism
LIST.DESC: Protects against burglary or intentional damage to your unit and belongings. Coverage includes repairing damage, replacing stolen items, and restoring your condo to its pre-loss condition, safeguarding your home from financial loss.

LIST.TITLE: Windstorm and Hail Damage
LIST.DESC: Covers damage from windstorms, hail, or flying debris that can affect your condo structure or personal belongings. This ensures costly repairs and replacements are handled, providing financial protection against unpredictable and severe weather.

LIST.TITLE: Plumbing and Electrical Damage
LIST.DESC: Protects your unit from unexpected plumbing leaks, burst pipes, and electrical malfunctions. Coverage helps repair water damage, replace wiring or appliances, and ensures your home remains safe and functional without costly expenses.

LIST.TITLE: Short-Term Rental Coverage (Airbnb/VRBO)
LIST.DESC: Provides protection for condos rented through VRBO or other short-term rental platforms. Coverage includes property damage, liability claims, and loss of rental income, ensuring hosts are fully safeguarded while their unit is occupied by guests.

LIST.TITLE: Pet Liability Coverage
LIST.DESC: Covers injuries or property damage caused by pets inside your condo. Liability coverage helps pay for medical bills, repair costs, or legal fees if your animal causes harm, ensuring you are protected from financial responsibility as a pet owner.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Condo Insurance NOT Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: The cost of condo insurance in Texas depends on multiple factors, including your unit's size, location, coverage limits, deductible choice, and the value of personal belongings. Average annual premiums range from $200 to $600, while optional coverage for high-value items, liability, or short-term rentals can increase the cost, but brokers can help find a plan tailored to your exact needs.

FLOOD_DAMAGE.TITLE: Flood Damage
FLOOD_DAMAGE.DESC: Condo insurance typically does not cover damage caused by floods. To protect against rising waters, heavy rain, or storm surges, a separate flood insurance policy is required. Without it, water damage from floods could cause repair costs.

EARTHQUAKE_DAMAGE.TITLE: Earthquake Damage
EARTHQUAKE_DAMAGE.DESC: Standard condo insurance policies exclude damage caused by earthquakes. If you live in an area prone to seismic activity, you must purchase a separate earthquake policy. This ensures that structural and personal property damage from tremors.

PEST_DAMAGE.TITLE: Pest and Termite Infestations
PEST_DAMAGE.DESC: Damage from pests, termites, or rodents is not covered under typical condo insurance. Repairs for infestations or structural harm caused by insects or rodents are the owner's responsibility, so regular inspections and pest control are essential.

WEAR_TEAR.TITLE: Wear and Tear / General Maintenance
WEAR_TEAR.DESC: Damage from pests, termites, or rodents is not covered under typical condo insurance. Repairs for infestations or structural harm caused by insects or rodents are the owner's responsibility, so regular inspections and pest control are essential.

MOLD_MILDEW.TITLE: Mold and Mildew (in most cases)
MOLD_MILDEW.DESC: Most condo insurance policies do not cover mold or mildew damage unless it is the direct result of a covered peril, such as a burst pipe. Prevention is crucial, as mold cleanup can be expensive and is generally excluded from standard coverage.

COMMON_AREAS.TITLE: Shared Common Areas (Covered by Your HOA)
COMMON_AREAS.DESC: Damage to shared areas like hallways, lobbies, roofs, or swimming pools is covered, not your personal condo insurance. Owners are responsible for the interior unit and personal belongings, while common spaces remain the HOA's responsibility.

INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE.TITLE: Intentional Damage
INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE.DESC: Condo insurance excludes intentional or malicious damage caused by the owner or residents. If you intentionally cause damage, your insurer will not pay for repairs, replacements, or liability, leaving you fully responsible for restoring the property.

BUSINESS_PROPERTY.TITLE: Business Equipment and Liability
BUSINESS_PROPERTY.DESC: Standard condo insurance does not cover business-related equipment claims. If you run a business from your condo, equipment, inventory, or client injuries are your responsibility unless a separate commercial policy or endorsement is purchased.

GOVERNMENT_SEIZURE.TITLE: Government Seizure or Demolition
GOVERNMENT_SEIZURE.DESC: Damage caused by government action, or demolition, is not covered by standard condo insurance. If authorities require property removal, demolition, or legal action affecting your unit, you will need special coverage or bear the costs personally.

WAR_NUCLEAR.TITLE: Nuclear Hazard or War
WAR_NUCLEAR.DESC: Events caused by nuclear accidents, radiation, or acts of war are excluded from condo insurance. Damage, destruction, or liability resulting from these extreme events is not covered, leaving owners responsible for losses unless specialized policies are obtained.

HIGH_VALUE_LIMITS.TITLE: Expensive Jewelry or Art (Above Policy Limits)
HIGH_VALUE_LIMITS.DESC: Condo insurance sets limits for high-value items. Expensive jewelry, fine art, or collectibles exceeding these limits are not fully covered. Owners must purchase additional riders or endorsements to ensure such valuables are protected against theft.

VEHICLE_DAMAGE.TITLE: Vehicles (Including Golf Carts and Motorcycles)
VEHICLE_DAMAGE.DESC: Standard condo insurance does not cover vehicles, including cars, motorcycles, or golf carts. Coverage for these requires an auto or specialized vehicle policy. Any damage or theft to vehicles on the property is not included in your condo plan.

PET_DAMAGE.TITLE: Damage from Pets
PET_DAMAGE.DESC: While some liability coverage exists, direct damage to personal property or the unit caused by pets is usually excluded. Chewing, scratching, or other intentional damage to the pet is the owner's responsibility and must be repaired at their own expense.

SINKHOLES.TITLE: Sinkholes (Unless Added as Endorsement)
SINKHOLES.DESC: Sinkhole damage is not included in standard condo insurance unless a specific endorsement is purchased. Structural collapse or ground shifts caused by sinkholes are excluded, making additional coverage necessary for properties in high-risk areas.

POWER_OUTAGE.TITLE: Power Outages and Utility Failures
POWER_OUTAGE.DESC: Condo insurance does not cover loss or damage from power outages or utility failures. Spoiled food, lost electronics, or inconvenience due to extended blackouts are the owner's responsibility unless separate equipment or outage coverage is purchased.

COST.TITLE: How Much Does Condo Insurance Cost in Texas?
COST.DESC1: Condo insurance costs in Texas can vary widely based on your coverage limits, deductible, location, and insurer. According to data from Insure, the average annual cost of condo insurance in Texas is about $1,007 per year ($84 per month) for a typical policy with $60,000 in personal property coverage and $300,000 in liability coverage. Rates can be higher or lower depending on your unit's specifics and the carrier you choose.
COST.DESC2: When comparing Texas condo insurance costs with other states, Texas tends to be above the national average, which is about $656 per year nationwide for similar coverage levels. This means Texas condo owners often pay more than residents of many other states, largely due to regional risks and rebuilding costs. Shopping around and comparing multiple insurers helps you find a competitive rate that fits your budget.

Check local brokers for updated quotes and discounts.

COMPANIES.TITLE: Average Condo Insurance Rates by Insurance Company in Texas
COMPANIES.DESC: Average condo insurance premiums in Texas differ by insurance company. For example, Farmers averages about $619 per year, State Farm around $874, Allstate about $808, Progressive roughly $1,427, Nationwide near $1,203, and USAA at around $1,137 annually. These figures reflect typical condo coverage costs across major insurers in Texas and help homeowners make informed, confident decisions.

HOW_MUCH_CONDO.TITLE: How Much Condo Insurance Do You Actually Need?
HOW_MUCH_CONDO.DESC1: Determining how much condo insurance you actually need starts with evaluating the value of your personal belongings and the interior of your unit. You should calculate the approximate cost to replace furniture, electronics, clothing, and other personal property if they were damaged or stolen. In addition, interior structure coverage, sometimes called walls-in coverage, should be enough to repair or replace anything inside your unit that isn't covered by your HOA's master policy, such as cabinets, flooring, fixtures, and built-in appliances.
HOW_MUCH_CONDO.DESC2: Liability protection is another essential factor in deciding your coverage level. Most experts recommend at least $300,000 in liability limits, but you might choose higher limits if you have significant assets to protect or frequently host guests. Additional endorsements, such as loss-of-use coverage, identity theft protection, or replacement-cost coverage for valuables, can also be tailored to your lifestyle and financial situation. Working with a licensed broker ensures you find the right balance between adequate protection and affordable premiums.

HEADER.DESC: Several factors affect your condo insurance rates in Texas, including your unit's location and proximity to flood zones or coastal areas, the building's age and construction type, your coverage limits and deductible choices, your credit history, claims history, and the value of your personal property. Insurers also consider local crime rates and the availability of fire protection when setting premiums.

CLAIMS_HISTORY.TITLE: Your Claims History

HEADER.TITLE: Independent Insurance Agency vs. Captive Agent: Why Choice Saves You Money
HEADER.DESC: Choosing between an independent insurance agency and a captive agent can significantly impact your condo insurance costs. WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.TITLE: What is Manufactured Home / Mobile Home Insurance and Why Do You Need It?
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC: Manufactured home or mobile home insurance is designed to protect your home from various risks, such as damage, theft, or accidents. Whether you own a mobile home, manufactured home, or modular home, this insurance provides coverage for both the structure and personal property within. It’s similar to homeowner’s insurance but tailored for homes that may not be permanently fixed to a foundation or are built to different standards.
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC1: Here are a few reasons why you need manufactured/mobile home insurance:

LIST.TITLE: Protection Against Natural Disasters
LIST.TEXT: The US is no stranger to extreme weather conditions, including windstorms, hail, and even flooding in certain areas. Manufactured home insurance helps cover damages caused by these disasters, ensuring your home stays protected even in the harshest weather conditions.

LIST.TITLE: Coverage for Your Property and Belongings
LIST.TEXT: Beyond the home’s structure, this insurance also covers personal property inside your home, such as furniture, electronics, and clothing. In the event of theft, vandalism, or damage, your belongings are protected, giving you peace of mind.

LIST.TITLE: Liability Coverage
LIST.TEXT: If someone is injured on your property, manufactured home insurance can cover medical expenses and potential legal costs if you're found liable. This is especially important if you have guests, pets, or children playing on your property.

LIST.TITLE: Fire and Smoke Protection
LIST.TEXT: Fires can be devastating, especially in homes not built to the same standards as traditional homes. Manufactured home insurance can cover fire damage to the structure and property, as well as the costs associated with smoke and water damage from firefighting efforts.

LIST.TITLE: Peace of Mind
LIST.TEXT: Finally, having mobile home or manufactured home insurance offers peace of mind. Knowing that your home and belongings are protected allows you to focus on living your life without the constant worry of unexpected accidents or disasters. This insurance is an investment in your home’s future.

MANUFACTURED_REQUIRED.TITLE: Is Manufactured Home / Mobile Home Insurance Required in Texas?
MANUFACTURED_REQUIRED.DESC1: In Texas, manufactured home or mobile home insurance is not legally required, but it may be necessary depending on your situation. If you own the home outright and it's not financed, you are not obligated to carry insurance. However, it's strongly recommended to protect your investment, especially with the risks posed by Texas weather and other unforeseen events.
MANUFACTURED_REQUIRED.DESC2: If your manufactured home is financed, your lender will likely require you to carry insurance. Lenders want to ensure their investment is protected, so they may mandate that you carry a policy that covers the home’s structure and any additional requirements, such as liability coverage. Even if you don't have a mortgage, securing insurance gives you peace of mind in the event of disasters like storms, fire, or theft.

MOBILE_VS_MANUFACTURED.TITLE: Is a Manufactured Home the Same as a Mobile Home?
MOBILE_VS_MANUFACTURED.DESC: A manufactured home and a mobile home may seem similar, but they are not really the same. Mobile homes were built before June 15, 1976, and didn’t follow a federal building standard. Manufactured homes, on the other hand, were built after that date and must comply with the HUD Code, a set of strict regulations ensuring better construction quality, safety, and energy efficiency.

LEGAL_CLASSIFICATION.MANUFACTURED: Can be titled as real property

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Manufactured Home / Mobile Home Insurance Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Manufactured home or mobile home insurance in Texas covers various aspects of your home and belongings. It includes dwelling coverage for the structure, personal property coverage for your belongings inside, and liability coverage in the event of an accident. It also protects against damage from fire, theft, vandalism, storms, and even accidents during transport, ensuring your home is protected.

STANDARD.TITLE: Standard Coverages (Included in Most Policies)
STANDARD.DESC: Most manufactured home policies include essential protections that cover the structure, personal property, liability risks, and temporary living expenses.

LIST.TITLE: Dwelling Coverage (The Structure of Your Home)
LIST.DESC: Dwelling coverage protects the structure of your manufactured or mobile home against damage caused by covered perils, such as fire, storms, or vandalism. It ensures that the main living space is rebuilt or repaired, safeguarding your investment.

LIST.TITLE: Other Structures Coverage (Sheds, Carports, Fences)
LIST.DESC: Other structures coverage extends protection to buildings on your property that aren’t attached to your home, such as sheds, carports, or fences. If these structures are damaged by a covered event, this coverage will help repair or replace them.

LIST.TITLE: Personal Property Coverage
LIST.DESC: Personal property coverage safeguards the items inside your manufactured home, such as furniture, electronics, and clothing. In the event of theft, fire, or a natural disaster, this coverage ensures you can replace your belongings.

LIST.TITLE: Personal Liability Coverage
LIST.DESC: This coverage helps protect you financially if someone is injured while on your property. It covers medical expenses and legal fees if you are held responsible. This type of coverage can prevent major financial setbacks in the event of a lawsuit.

LIST.TITLE: Medical Payments to Others
LIST.DESC: It helps pay for medical costs if someone is injured on your property, regardless of fault. This coverage is typically limited to smaller amounts and is designed to cover immediate medical needs without requiring a lawsuit or a lengthy process.

LIST.TITLE: Loss of Use / Additional Living Expenses
LIST.DESC: If your home becomes uninhabitable due to a covered event, loss-of-use or additional living expenses coverage will help pay for temporary living arrangements. This includes hotel stays, meals, and other expenses, so you can maintain your lifestyle.

LIST.TITLE: Trip Collision Coverage (While Being Transported)
LIST.DESC: It covers damage to your home during transport, whether it’s caused by an accident or other unforeseen incidents. This comprehensive coverage ensures that you’re not left financially vulnerable during the relocation process.

LIST.TITLE: Attached Structures (Decks, Porches, Awnings)
LIST.DESC: Attached structures coverage protects additions to the home, such as decks, porches, and awnings, against damage from events like storms, fires, or accidents. If these parts of your home are damaged, this helps pay for repairs or replacements.

LIST.TITLE: Fire and Smoke Damage
LIST.DESC: This helps repair or replace your home and belongings if they are damaged by fire or smoke. It covers the cost of rebuilding your home and replacing items that have been burned or damaged by smoke, ensuring you can recover from these events.

LIST.TITLE: Windstorm and Hail Damage
LIST.DESC: This is essential in areas like Texas, where severe storms are common. This coverage protects your home from damage caused by high winds, hail, or tornadoes, including repairs to the structure and personal property affected by these events.

LIST.TITLE: Theft and Vandalism
LIST.DESC: It helps protect your home and belongings from damage or loss caused by criminal activity. Whether someone breaks into your home or damages your property, this ensures you can repair or replace items and restore your home to its previous condition.

LIST.TITLE: Plumbing and Electrical Damage
LIST.DESC: It pays for repairs to your home’s plumbing or electrical systems if they are damaged by a covered event, like a burst pipe or electrical fire. This ensures that issues with these vital systems are fixed without causing a significant financial burden.

LIST.TITLE: Water Backup and Sump Pump Overflow
LIST.DESC: Water backup and sump pump overflow coverage helps protect against damage caused by water backing up into your home through drains, sewers, or sump pumps. This can include damage to flooring, walls, and personal belongings, offering peace of mind.

LIST.TITLE: Falling Objects Coverage
LIST.DESC: Falling objects coverage provides protection if objects, such as tree branches or debris, fall and damage your home or personal property. Whether it's caused by severe weather or an accident, this coverage ensures that you can repair or replace.

LIST.TITLE: Explosion Coverage
LIST.DESC: Explosion coverage protects your manufactured home against damage from explosions, such as gas leaks or nearby industrial incidents. This coverage helps repair your home and replace personal property that may be destroyed in the event of a blast.

LIST.TITLE: Riot and Civil Commotion Coverage
LIST.DESC: Riot and civil commotion coverage helps cover damages caused by riots, looting, or civil disturbances. If your manufactured home is damaged during a protest or public unrest, this coverage helps you repair or replace the affected areas.

LIST.TITLE: Refrigerated Property Coverage
LIST.DESC: This ensures that food, beverages, or other items stored in refrigerators or freezers are protected if damaged by a covered event. This is useful for homes in areas where power disruptions can cause loss of refrigerated goods.

LIST.TITLE: Debris Removal Coverage
LIST.DESC: It pays for the cost of clearing debris from your property after a covered event. If your home or yard is littered with fallen trees, broken pieces, or damaged materials, this coverage helps you remove the debris, so repairs can begin promptly.

LIST.TITLE: Identity Theft Coverage
LIST.DESC: Identity theft coverage protects you if someone uses your personal information to commit fraud or steal your identity. This covers the costs of restoring your identity, including legal fees, lost wages, and the cost of fixing any damage caused.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Manufactured Home / Mobile Home Insurance NOT Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Manufactured home or mobile home insurance in Texas does not cover certain risks that could cause damage. These typically include flood and earthquake damage, wear and tear, pest infestations, and mold. It also doesn't cover intentional damage, business-related losses, or damage to vehicles. Certain exclusions may be added with endorsements for additional protection.

FLOOD_DAMAGE.TITLE: Flood Damage
FLOOD_DAMAGE.DESC: Standard manufactured home insurance policies do not cover flood damage. If you live in an area prone to flooding, you will need to secure separate flood insurance to protect your home from water damage by heavy rainfall or rising water levels.

EARTHQUAKE_DAMAGE.TITLE: Earthquake Damage
EARTHQUAKE_DAMAGE.DESC: Earthquake-related damage is excluded from most home insurance policies. To cover the risk of ground shaking, cracks, and other seismic damage, you’ll need to purchase an earthquake endorsement or a separate earthquake insurance policy.

PEST_DAMAGE.TITLE: Pest and Termite Infestations
PEST_DAMAGE.DESC: Most manufactured home insurance policies do not include coverage for damage caused by pests such as termites or rodents. Since pest infestations result from ongoing maintenance issues, they are considered the homeowner’s responsibility.

WEAR_TEAR.TITLE: Wear and Tear / General Maintenance
WEAR_TEAR.DESC: Insurance does not cover the normal wear and tear of your home or its components. Routine maintenance, such as roof repairs or appliance replacements, is the homeowner’s responsibility and cannot be covered under standard insurance policies.

MOLD_MILDEW.TITLE: Mold and Mildew (in most cases)
MOLD_MILDEW.DESC: Mold and mildew are usually not covered unless they result from a sudden and accidental event, such as a burst pipe. Most policies exclude mold damage, so regular maintenance to prevent moisture buildup is essential to avoid mold growth in your home.

INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE.TITLE: Intentional Damage
INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE.DESC: Damage caused intentionally by the homeowner or others is not covered by insurance. Any harm to your home or belongings that results from deliberate actions, whether vandalism or self-inflicted destruction, will not be reimbursed by your policy.

VACANT_DAMAGE.TITLE: Vacant Home Damage (If Unoccupied Too Long)
VACANT_DAMAGE.DESC: Damage to vacant homes is typically excluded if the home has been unoccupied for an extended period. If your home remains empty for more than 30 days, you'll need a special vacant-home endorsement to maintain coverage for risks such as theft or vandalism.

BUSINESS_PROPERTY.TITLE: Business Equipment and Liability
BUSINESS_PROPERTY.DESC: Home insurance does not cover business-related equipment or liabilities. If you operate a business from your home, you will need a separate commercial policy to protect your business assets, liabilities, and any damages from business activities.

VEHICLE_DAMAGE.TITLE: Vehicles (Including Golf Carts and ATVs)
VEHICLE_DAMAGE.DESC: Policies for manufactured homes do not cover vehicles such as cars, golf carts, or ATVs. These vehicles require separate coverage under auto or recreational vehicle policies, as home insurance only covers the structure and personal property.

PET_DAMAGE.TITLE: Damage from Pets
PET_DAMAGE.DESC: Damage caused by pets, such as chewed furniture or scratched floors, is generally not covered under home insurance policies. However, if your pet injures someone else, personal liability coverage may protect you from potential lawsuits.

SINKHOLES.TITLE: Sinkholes (Unless Added as Endorsement)
SINKHOLES.DESC: Sinkhole damage is typically excluded from standard coverage. If you live in an area prone to sinkholes, you may need to purchase an endorsement or additional coverage to protect your home.

POWER_OUTAGE.TITLE: Power Outages and Utility Failures
POWER_OUTAGE.DESC: Damage caused by power outages or utility failures is not covered by home insurance. If your refrigerator spoils during a power outage or your plumbing freezes, you’ll need to pay out of pocket unless you add specific coverage.

WAR_NUCLEAR.TITLE: Nuclear Hazard or War
WAR_NUCLEAR.DESC: Home insurance policies do not cover damages caused by nuclear accidents or acts of war. These events are considered catastrophic and outside the scope of coverage, with no provisions available to protect homes in such circumstances.

GOVERNMENT_SEIZURE.TITLE: Government Seizure or Demolition
GOVERNMENT_SEIZURE.DESC: Damage or loss resulting from government seizure or property demolition is excluded. If your home is seized for public use or demolished due to governmental actions, you won’t receive compensation through your standard insurance policy.

LANDSLIDE.TITLE: Landslide and Earth Movement
LANDSLIDE.DESC: Damage from landslides and earth movements, such as soil erosion or shifting ground, is not covered by standard manufactured home insurance. You may need additional coverage or endorsements if your home is in a high-risk area.

SEWER_BACKUP.TITLE: Sewer Backup (Unless Added as Endorsement)
SEWER_BACKUP.DESC: Sewer backup damage is excluded unless you purchase a specific endorsement. This insurance coverage protects you from water damage caused by backed-up sewer lines, which can flood your home with waste and cause costly repairs.

HIGH_VALUE_LIMITS.TITLE: Expensive Jewelry or Art (Above Policy Limits)
HIGH_VALUE_LIMITS.DESC: High-value items such as jewelry, fine art, or collectibles may exceed the coverage limits of your standard home policy. For full protection, consider adding a personal property rider or additional coverage to safeguard expensive possessions.

TRANSPORT_DAMAGE.TITLE: Damage During Transport (Unless Trip Collision is Added)
TRANSPORT_DAMAGE.DESC: Damage that occurs during the transport of your manufactured home is generally not covered unless trip collision coverage is added. This protects your home during the moving process, covering damages from accidents or other incidents during transport.

NON_HUD.TITLE: Homes Not Built to HUD Code
NON_HUD.DESC: Homes not built to the HUD Code (pre-1976) are often excluded from standard manufactured home insurance. These homes do not meet federal building standards and may not qualify for certain coverages available under modern policies.

BUSINESS_USE.TITLE: Homes Used for Business Purposes
BUSINESS_USE.DESC: Homes used for business purposes are generally not covered under standard home insurance policies. If you operate a business from home, you will need commercial coverage to protect your business equipment, operations, and any related liabilities.

COST.TITLE: How Much Does Manufactured Home / Mobile Home Insurance Cost in Texas?
COST.DESC1: Manufactured home and mobile home insurance costs in Texas can vary widely based on your home’s size, age, location, and coverage choices. On average, Texans pay between $1,500 and $1,800 per year for a typical mobile or manufactured home insurance policy. In some higher-risk areas, such as near the Gulf Coast or Tornado Alley, annual premiums often range from $1,500 to $2,700 or more.
COST.DESC2: When comparing Texas to other states, Texas manufactured home insurance costs tend to be higher than the national average for mobile homes due to extreme weather risks like hail, windstorms, and hurricanes. States with milder weather and less severe storm activity typically offer lower premiums, while storm‑prone states like Florida or coastal regions often have similar or even higher rates.

HOW_MUCH_MANUFACTURED.TITLE: How Much Manufactured Home Insurance Do You Actually Need?
HOW_MUCH_MANUFACTURED.DESC1: The amount of manufactured home insurance you need depends on factors such as your home's value, the contents inside, and your location. A standard policy typically covers the home's structure, personal property, and liability protection. However, if you live in an area prone to natural disasters like floods or hurricanes, you may need additional coverage for specific risks that aren’t included in a basic policy. It’s important to assess the risks in your area and adjust your coverage accordingly.
HOW_MUCH_MANUFACTURED.DESC2: When determining how much insurance to buy, consider the replacement cost of your home and personal belongings. You want enough coverage to rebuild your home in the event of a total loss and replace your valuables. Additionally, if your home is in a mobile home park or you have special features or upgrades, these should be factored into your policy. Working with an insurance agent can help ensure you have the right amount of coverage tailored to your specific needs.

HEADER.TITLE: Factors That Impact Your Manufactured Home / Mobile Home Insurance Rates in Texas
HEADER.DESC: Several factors impact the cost of manufactured home or mobile home insurance rates in Texas. These include your home's age, size, location, and type of construction. Additional factors like the proximity to flood zones, the risk of windstorms, and whether your home is on a permanent foundation can also influence the overall premium.

LOCATION.TITLE: Location of Your Home
LOCATION.DESC: Homes in high-risk areas, such as flood zones or tornado paths, have higher premiums. Location affects coverage costs significantly.

AGE.TITLE: Age of Your Manufactured Home
AGE.DESC: Older homes often have higher rates due to increased risk of wear, outdated materials, or safety concerns.

SIZE.TITLE: Size of Your Home (Single-Wide vs. Double-Wide vs. Triple-Wide)
SIZE.DESC: Larger homes generally cost more to insure due to higher replacement costs for repairs or damage.

CONSTRUCTION.TITLE: Construction Material and Quality
CONSTRUCTION.DESC: Homes built with higher-quality materials or stronger construction standards may have lower premiums due to greater durability.

HUD_COMPLIANCE.TITLE: HUD Code Compliance
HUD_COMPLIANCE.DESC: Homes built after 1976 to meet the HUD Code generally have lower rates due to higher safety and construction standards.

FOUNDATION.TITLE: Whether Your Home is on a Permanent Foundation
FOUNDATION.DESC: Homes on a permanent foundation are less likely to be damaged during severe weather, which can reduce insurance premiums.

LAND_OWNERSHIP.TITLE: Whether You Own or Lease the Land
LAND_OWNERSHIP.DESC: Owning the land reduces risk for insurers, lowering your premiums. Leasing land may increase coverage costs.

COAST_PROXIMITY.TITLE: Proximity to Coast or Flood Zones
COAST_PROXIMITY.DESC: Homes near the coast or in flood-prone areas face higher rates due to the increased risk of water damage.

WINDSTORM_RISK.TITLE: Windstorm and Hurricane Risk in Your Area
WINDSTORM_RISK.DESC: If your home is in an area with high wind or hurricane risk, expect higher premiums to cover storm-related damages.

CRIME_RATE.TITLE: Crime Rate in Your Area
CRIME_RATE.DESC: Living in a higher-crime area can lead to higher premiums as insurers account for the increased risk of theft and vandalism.

FIRE_STATION_DISTANCE.TITLE: Distance to Nearest Fire Station
FIRE_STATION_DISTANCE.DESC: Homes farther from fire stations may face higher premiums due to the longer response times during emergencies.

FIRE_FEATURES.TITLE: Fire Protection Features (Smoke Detectors, Sprinklers)
FIRE_FEATURES.DESC: Homes equipped with smoke detectors or sprinklers may have lower rates because these systems reduce the risk of fire damage.

SECURITY_FEATURES.TITLE: Security Features (Alarms, Deadbolts, Cameras)
SECURITY_FEATURES.DESC: Homes with security features such as alarms or cameras are less likely to be burglarized, which can lower premiums.

TIE_DOWNS.TITLE: Storm Tie-Downs and Anchoring System
TIE_DOWNS.DESC: Homes with storm tie-downs or anchoring systems are more secure during high winds, often resulting in lower rates.

ROOF_CONDITION.TITLE: Roof Age and Condition
ROOF_CONDITION.DESC: Older or damaged roofs may lead to higher rates due to the increased risk of leaks or collapse during severe weather.

COVERAGE_AMOUNT.TITLE: Coverage Amount You Choose
COVERAGE_AMOUNT.DESC: Higher coverage limits increase premiums since the insurer will pay more in the event of a claim or disaster.

DEDUCTIBLE.TITLE: Your Deductible Amount
DEDUCTIBLE.DESC: A higher deductible generally lowers premiums, as the homeowner assumes more of the initial repair costs.

CLAIMS_HISTORY.TITLE: Your Claims History
CLAIMS_HISTORY.DESC: A history of frequent claims can lead to higher premiums, as insurers consider you a higher risk for future claims.

CREDIT_SCORE.TITLE: Your Credit Score
CREDIT_SCORE.DESC: A higher credit score may lower premiums, as insurers use credit as an indicator of financial responsibility.

RENTAL_STATUS.TITLE: Whether You Rent Out Your Home
RENTAL_STATUS.DESC: Renting out your home may increase premiums due to higher liability risks and potential damage from tenants.

PARK_STATUS.TITLE: Whether the Home is in a Mobile Home Park
PARK_STATUS.DESC: Homes in mobile home parks may face higher premiums due to greater density and potential shared risks.

BUNDLING.TITLE: Bundling With Other Policies (Auto, Life, etc.)
BUNDLING.DESC: Bundling multiple policies with the same insurer can result in discounts, lowering your overall premium costs.

CARRIER.TITLE: Insurance Carrier You Choose
CARRIER.DESC: Different insurers have varying rates and coverage options, so comparing companies can help find the best deal.

RESIDENCY_TYPE.TITLE: Whether the Home is Used as a Primary or Secondary Residence
RESIDENCY_TYPE.DESC: Secondary homes may have higher premiums due to the increased risk of damage from long periods of vacancy.

TRIP_COLLISION_RISK.TITLE: Trip Collision Risk (If Home is Moved Frequently)
TRIP_COLLISION_RISK.DESC: Homes moved frequently for relocation may have higher premiums due to the risk of damage during transport or collisions.

HEADER.TITLE: How to Maximize Your Discounts and Lower Your Premium
HEADER.DESC: To maximize your discounts and lower your premium, consider bundling your manufactured home insurance with other policies, like auto or life insurance, to receive multi-policy discounts. Installing security systems, fire alarms, and storm tie-downs can also reduce rates. Maintaining a clean claims history and opting for a higher deductible can further help you save on your premium.

BUNDLING.TITLE: Multi-Policy / Bundling Discount
BUNDLING.DESC: Combine policies, such as auto and life insurance, to receive a multi-policy discount and lower your overall premiums.

CLAIM_FREE.TITLE: Claims-Free Discount
CLAIM_FREE.DESC: Maintain a claims-free record to earn discounts, as insurers reward low-risk, claim-free customers.

LOYALTY.TITLE: Loyalty Discount
LOYALTY.DESC: Staying with the same insurer for multiple years may qualify you for loyalty discounts on your premiums.

NEW_HOME.TITLE: New Manufactured Home Discount
NEW_HOME.DESC: Newer homes often qualify for policy discounts due to improved construction, safety, and energy efficiency.

NEW_ROOF.TITLE: New Roof Discount
NEW_ROOF.DESC: A newly installed roof may lower your insurance premium because it reduces the risk of damage during storms.

PERMANENT_FOUNDATION.TITLE: Permanent Foundation Discount
PERMANENT_FOUNDATION.DESC: Homes on permanent foundations may receive a discount on their policy because they are more stable in severe weather.

STORM_TIE_DOWNS.TITLE: Storm Tie-Down and Anchoring Discount
STORM_TIE_DOWNS.DESC: Securely anchored homes are less vulnerable during high winds, often leading to lower insurance rates.

WIND_MITIGATION.TITLE: Wind Mitigation / Storm Shutters Discount
WIND_MITIGATION.DESC: Adding storm shutters or other wind-resistant features can help reduce premiums in wind-prone areas.

SECURITY_SYSTEM.TITLE: Security System Discount
SECURITY_SYSTEM.DESC: Homes with security systems, such as alarms or cameras, are considered lower risk and receive a discounted policy.

SMOKE_DETECTOR.TITLE: Smoke Detector and Fire Alarm Discount
SMOKE_DETECTOR.DESC: Installing smoke detectors or fire alarms can lower insurance premiums by reducing fire-related risks.

SPRINKLER_SYSTEM.TITLE: Sprinkler System Discount
SPRINKLER_SYSTEM.DESC: Installing a sprinkler system can reduce fire damage costs and potentially lower your insurance premiums.

DEADBOLT.TITLE: Deadbolt and Door Lock Discount
DEADBOLT.DESC: Upgrading to deadbolts and stronger locks can reduce theft risks, leading to discounts on your premiums.

GATED_COMMUNITY.TITLE: Gated Community / Mobile Home Park Discount
GATED_COMMUNITY.DESC: Living in a gated community or mobile home park may lower premiums due to the reduced risk of theft.

NON_SMOKER.TITLE: Non-Smoker Discount
NON_SMOKER.DESC: Non-smokers often receive insurance discounts, as smoking increases the risk of fire-related damage in homes.

GOOD_CREDIT.TITLE: Good Credit Discount
GOOD_CREDIT.DESC: A good credit score is often rewarded with lower premiums, as insurers view financially responsible customers as lower risk.

PAPERLESS.TITLE: Paperless Billing Discount
PAPERLESS.DESC: Opting for paperless billing can earn discounts on insurance policies as insurers save on administrative costs.

AUTO_PAY.TITLE: Auto-Pay Discount
AUTO_PAY.DESC: Paying your premium automatically can save you money, as insurers offer discounts for consistent payments.

PAID_FULL.TITLE: Pay-in-Full Discount
PAID_FULL.DESC: Paying your insurance premium upfront, rather than in installments, may qualify you for a discount.

HIGH_DEDUCTIBLE.TITLE: Higher Deductible Discount
