WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.TITLE: What is Landlord Insurance and Why Do You Need It?
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC: Landlord insurance is a specialized type of coverage designed for property owners who rent out their homes, apartments, or commercial spaces. Unlike standard homeowners insurance, it protects both the building and landlords' financial interests, including potential loss of rental income and liability claims from tenants or visitors. This insurance ensures that property owners are safeguarded against common risks associated with rental properties.

LIST.TITLE: Protection for Your Property
LIST.TEXT: The core benefit of landlord insurance is coverage for physical damage to your property. Whether caused by fire, storms, vandalism, or accidental tenant damage, this insurance helps repair or replace your property without a heavy financial burden.

LIST.TITLE: Liability Coverage
LIST.TEXT: Landlord insurance also provides liability protection in case someone is injured on your property. If a tenant, guest, or visitor suffers an accident and files a claim, this coverage can protect you from legal expenses and potential settlements.

LIST.TITLE: Loss of Rental Income
LIST.TEXT: If your rental property becomes uninhabitable due to damage from a covered event, landlord insurance can replace lost rental income. This ensures you continue to meet financial obligations, such as mortgage payments, even during unexpected interruptions.

LIST.TITLE: Additional Coverage Options
LIST.TEXT: Many landlord insurance policies offer optional add-ons for extra protection. This can include coverage for landlord-owned contents, legal expenses, or even certain natural disasters, allowing you to customize your plan based on your property and risk profile.

LIST.TITLE: Tenant-Related Risk Protection
LIST.TEXT: Landlord insurance may also help cover risks tied to tenant-related issues, such as accidental damage or certain disputes. While coverage varies by policy, having this protection adds an extra layer of security, helping landlords manage unexpected situations.

LANDLORD_REQUIRED.TITLE: Is Landlord Insurance Required in Texas?
LANDLORD_REQUIRED.DESC1: Landlord insurance is not legally required in Texas, but it is highly recommended for property owners who rent out their homes or apartments. While Texas law does not mandate landlords to carry insurance, having a policy in place protects you from financial losses due to property damage, liability claims, or loss of rental income. Without coverage, you could face significant out-of-pocket expenses if unexpected events like fire, storms, or tenant accidents occur.
LANDLORD_REQUIRED.DESC2: Even though it isn’t required, many lenders and mortgage companies strongly encourage or require landlords to maintain insurance as a condition for financing. Protecting your investment with landlord insurance ensures your property, income, and peace of mind are safeguarded. It also demonstrates responsibility to tenants, providing confidence that their rented space is well managed and that both parties are protected in the event of unforeseen circumstances.

HOMEOWNERS_VS_LANDLORD.TITLE: Does My Homeowners Insurance Cover My Rental Property?
HOMEOWNERS_VS_LANDLORD.DESC1: Most standard homeowners' insurance policies do not cover rental properties or the risks associated with renting out your home. These policies are designed to protect owner-occupied residences, so using your home as a rental could leave you exposed to damage, liability claims, and loss of rental income. If a tenant causes accidental damage or someone gets injured on the property, a homeowner's policy may deny coverage, leaving you responsible for repair and legal costs.
HOMEOWNERS_VS_LANDLORD.DESC2: Because of these gaps, it’s important to have landlord insurance specifically for rental properties. This type of policy is designed to protect both the building and your financial interests by covering property damage, liability, and potential loss of income. By securing landlord insurance, you ensure your rental investment is properly protected while staying compliant with lender requirements and maintaining peace of mind.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Landlord Insurance Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Landlord insurance covers property damage from fire, storms, vandalism, or tenant accidents. It also provides liability protection if someone is injured on your rental, and can replace lost rental income if the property becomes uninhabitable. Optional add-ons insurance may cover landlord-owned contents, legal expenses, and other risks specific to rental properties.

STANDARD.TITLE: Standard Coverages (Included in Most Policies)
STANDARD.DESC: Most landlord insurance policies include essential protections that cover the structure, liability, loss of income, and landlord-owned property.

LIST.TITLE: Dwelling Coverage (The Structure of Your Rental Property)
LIST.DESC: Protects the main structure of your rental property, including walls, roof, floors, and built-in fixtures, from covered perils such as fire, storms, and vandalism, ensuring your investment is protected and that tenants have a safe, habitable home.

LIST.TITLE: Other Structures Coverage (Fences, Garages, Sheds)
LIST.DESC: Covers detached structures such as fences, garages, and sheds on your rental property, protecting them from fire, storms, vandalism, or other covered events, helping landlords maintain full property security and avoid costly repairs or replacements.

LIST.TITLE: Landlord Personal Property Coverage (Appliances, Furniture)
LIST.DESC: Protects landlord-owned items like appliances, furniture, and fixtures provided for tenant use, covering loss or damage from fire, theft, or accidents, ensuring tenants have functional amenities while landlords avoid out-of-pocket replacement costs.

LIST.TITLE: Rental Income Loss Coverage
LIST.DESC: Reimburses lost rental income if your property becomes uninhabitable due to covered damage, helping landlords continue paying mortgages, bills, and expenses while repairs are made, protecting financial stability and maintaining consistent cash flow.

LIST.TITLE: Personal Liability Coverage
LIST.DESC: Provides financial protection if a tenant, guest, or visitor is injured on your rental property, covering legal fees, settlements, or court costs, helping landlords manage liability risk while keeping personal and business finances secure.

LIST.TITLE: Medical Payments to Others
LIST.DESC: Pays medical expenses for guests injured on your property, regardless of fault, ensuring quick care, preventing disputes, and covering minor accidents efficiently, helping landlords maintain good tenant relations and avoid costly legal claims.

LIST.TITLE: Fire and Smoke Damage
LIST.DESC: Covers damage to your rental property and landlord-owned items caused by fire or smoke, including repairs and replacements, helping landlords restore the property safely and quickly while minimizing financial loss and tenant disruption.

LIST.TITLE: Windstorm and Hail Damage
LIST.DESC: Protects rental property from wind and hail damage, covering repairs to roofs, siding, and exterior structures, reducing costly out-of-pocket expenses, and helping landlords maintain property value after severe weather events.

LIST.TITLE: Theft and Vandalism
LIST.DESC: Covers losses or damage caused by theft, break-ins, or vandalism, protecting landlord-owned property and rental structures, helping landlords safeguard their investment while ensuring tenants’ living conditions remain secure and functional.

LIST.TITLE: Plumbing and Electrical Damage
LIST.DESC: Provides coverage for damage caused by plumbing or electrical system failures, such as leaks, clogs, or shorts, protecting rental property and landlord-owned items, minimizing repair costs, and preventing disruption for tenants.

LIST.TITLE: Water Backup and Sump Pump Overflow
LIST.DESC: Landlord insurance covers water damage from sewer backups or sump pump failures, protecting basements, flooring, and landlord-owned property, and helping landlords restore rental units quickly and avoid costly repairs or property loss.

LIST.TITLE: Falling Objects Coverage
LIST.DESC: Protects against damage from objects falling on your rental property, such as tree limbs, debris, or structural collapses, helping landlords maintain tenant safety and quickly repair property without bearing unexpected financial loss.

LIST.TITLE: Explosion Coverage
LIST.DESC: Covers damage caused by explosions, including gas leaks or accidental blasts, protecting both the structure and landlord-owned property, helping Texas landlords recover from sudden catastrophic events without significant out-of-pocket expense.

LIST.TITLE: Riot and Civil Commotion Coverage
LIST.DESC: Protects rental property against damage from riots, protests, or civil unrest, including vandalism and destruction, helping landlords recover costs, maintain security, and restore property quickly while minimizing financial impact.

LIST.TITLE: Debris Removal Coverage
LIST.DESC: Covers the costs of removing debris after a covered loss, such as fallen trees, building rubble, or hazardous materials, ensuring the rental property is cleared efficiently, repaired safely, and ready for tenants without an extra financial burden.

LIST.TITLE: Fair Rental Value Coverage
LIST.DESC: Reimburses lost rental income if the property is partially or fully uninhabitable due to a covered loss, helping landlords maintain cash flow, pay mortgages, and meet expenses while repairs restore the property for tenant occupancy.

LIST.TITLE: Eviction-Related Legal Expense Coverage
LIST.DESC: Covers legal expenses associated with evicting tenants, including non-payment or lease violations, helping landlords enforce agreements without financial strain while protecting their rental property and maintaining a fair and lawful rental process.

LIST.TITLE: Ordinance or Law Coverage (Code Upgrade After Loss)
LIST.DESC: Pays for necessary upgrades to meet current building codes after a covered loss, ensuring the rental property complies with regulations, reducing out-of-pocket repair costs, and keeping the property safe, functional, and legally compliant.

LIST.TITLE: Inflation Protection Coverage
LIST.DESC: Automatically increases coverage limits to account for inflation, ensuring landlord insurance remains adequate as costs for property repairs, rebuilding, or replacement of landlord-owned items rise, protecting your investment over time.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Landlord Insurance NOT Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Landlord insurance in Texas does not cover normal wear and tear, routine maintenance issues, or damage caused intentionally by tenants. Landlord insurance also generally excludes floods, earthquakes, and mold unless additional optional coverage is purchased. Knowing these insurance policy gaps helps landlords plan extra protection and avoid costly, unexpected, and long-term expenses.

TENANT_BELONGINGS.TITLE: Tenant's Personal Belongings
TENANT_BELONGINGS.DESC: Landlord insurance does not cover tenants’ personal belongings, such as furniture, electronics, or clothing. Tenants need renters insurance to protect their own property, separate from the landlord’s coverage, helping ensure their belongings are safe.

FLOOD_DAMAGE.TITLE: Flood Damage
FLOOD_DAMAGE.DESC: Standard landlord insurance policies do not cover flood damage. Property owners must purchase separate insurance to protect against rising waters, flash floods, or storm-related events, safeguarding structures and reducing financial risk.

EARTHQUAKE_DAMAGE.TITLE: Earthquake Damage
EARTHQUAKE_DAMAGE.DESC: Damage caused by earthquakes is not included in most landlord insurance policies. Property owners who want protection from seismic activity must add a separate earthquake endorsement to ensure their rental property is covered for these rare events.

PEST_DAMAGE.TITLE: Pest and Termite Infestations
PEST_DAMAGE.DESC: Infestations caused by pests, termites, or rodents are excluded. Landlords must handle prevention, treatment, and repairs themselves to avoid structural damage and maintain a safe, habitable rental property for tenants, especially for pests and termites.

WEAR_TEAR.TITLE: Wear and Tear / General Maintenance
WEAR_TEAR.DESC: Normal wear and tear, aging, or maintenance issues, such as worn carpets, peeling paint, or plumbing aging, are not covered. Landlords are responsible for routine upkeep and repairs to maintain property value and tenant safety.

MOLD_MILDEW.TITLE: Mold and Mildew (in most cases)
MOLD_MILDEW.DESC: Mold or mildew damage is usually excluded unless caused by a covered peril. Landlords should address moisture issues promptly and consider optional coverage to protect the property from costly mold and mildew remediation expenses.

INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE_LANDLORD.TITLE: Intentional Damage by Landlord
INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE_LANDLORD.DESC: Insurance policies do not cover damage caused intentionally by the landlord. Coverage applies only to accidents, natural disasters, or unforeseen events; any deliberate acts of damage are the property owner's responsibility.

VACANT_PROPERTY.TITLE: Vacant Property (After Extended Period)
VACANT_PROPERTY.DESC: Properties left vacant for a long period may not be covered. Landlords should either notify their insurer or purchase vacancy coverage to maintain coverage while the property is unoccupied, avoiding gaps in insurance.

SHORT_TERM_RENTAL_EXCLUSION.TITLE: Short-Term Rental Activity (Airbnb/VRBO) Without Endorsement
SHORT_TERM_RENTAL_EXCLUSION.DESC: Using a rental for short-term activity like Airbnb or VRBO is not covered unless an endorsement is added. Standard landlord insurance covers long-term tenants, so special short-term rental coverage is necessary to avoid denied claims.

BUSINESS_PROPERTY.TITLE: Business Equipment and Liability
BUSINESS_PROPERTY.DESC: Landlord insurance does not cover business equipment or liability. Owners operating a business on the property must have separate commercial coverage to protect inventory, equipment, and liability risks from business operations.

VEHICLE_DAMAGE.TITLE: Vehicles on the Property
VEHICLE_DAMAGE.DESC: Damage to vehicles on rental property is not covered. Cars, trucks, motorcycles, or other vehicles belong to tenants or owners and require separate auto insurance, as landlord policies only cover the building and specified landlord-owned property.

TENANT_DAMAGE.TITLE: Damage Caused by Tenants (in most cases)
TENANT_DAMAGE.DESC: Most landlord policies exclude damage caused intentionally or negligently by tenants. Landlords must pursue tenant-paid repairs or purchase optional coverage to protect the property from intentional or accidental tenant damage.

SINKHOLES.TITLE: Sinkholes (Unless Added as Endorsement)
SINKHOLES.DESC: Sinkhole damage is not included unless a specific endorsement is added. Landlords in areas with ground instability should purchase optional coverage to protect their property from costly subsidence and structural damage.

POWER_OUTAGE.TITLE: Power Outages and Utility Failures
POWER_OUTAGE.DESC: Landlord insurance does not cover losses caused by power outages, utility interruptions, or failures. Property owners cannot claim repair or income losses from temporary utility problems under standard insurance policies.

WAR_NUCLEAR.TITLE: Nuclear Hazard or War
WAR_NUCLEAR.DESC: Damage from nuclear events, radiation, or acts of war is excluded. Landlord insurance protects against common risks, but catastrophic global events are not covered, leaving property owners responsible for losses from extraordinary disasters.

GOVERNMENT_SEIZURE.TITLE: Government Seizure or Demolition
GOVERNMENT_SEIZURE.DESC: If a property is seized or demolished by a government authority, landlord insurance will not cover the loss. Property owners must rely on legal channels, government compensation programs, or other financial remedies for these events.

LANDSLIDE.TITLE: Landslide and Earth Movement
LANDSLIDE.DESC: Damage caused by landslides or earth movement is usually excluded. Landlords in areas prone to soil shifting or geological risks should consider optional endorsements to ensure adequate coverage for ground movement and structural damage.

SEWER_BACKUP.TITLE: Sewer Backup (Unless Added as Endorsement)
SEWER_BACKUP.DESC: Sewer backups and sump pump overflows are excluded unless an optional endorsement is purchased. Landlords should consider this sewer backup coverage to protect basements, flooring, and landlord-owned property from water damage.

HIGH_VALUE_LIMITS.TITLE: Expensive Landlord Property (Above Policy Limits)
HIGH_VALUE_LIMITS.DESC: High-value landlord-owned items above the policy limit are not fully covered. Property owners should review policy limits and consider endorsements for expensive appliances, electronics, or furniture to ensure adequate protection.

RENTAL_INCOME_NON_PAYMENT.TITLE: Loss of Rental Income Due to Tenant Non-Payment
RENTAL_INCOME_NON_PAYMENT.DESC: Standard rental income landlord insurance does not cover lost rental income from tenants failing to pay rent. Landlords should consider lease agreements, rent guarantee policies, or other measures to protect income if tenants default.

COST.TITLE: How Much Does Landlord Insurance Cost in Texas?
COST.DESC1: In Texas, the cost of landlord insurance varies based on property type, location, and coverage levels. On average, landlords can expect to pay between about $1,300 and $1,900 per year for a single‑family rental home, which breaks down to roughly $110–$160 per month for basic coverage. Larger or higher‑value properties may see premiums of $1,200–$4,000 or more annually, especially in urban or high‑risk areas with higher crime rates or weather-related exposure.
COST.DESC2: Compared with other states, landlord insurance costs can be higher or lower depending on regional risk factors. The national average landlord policy cost is around $1,516 per year, with some states like Rhode Island exceeding $2,400 annually and more affordable states like Oklahoma closer to $595 annually. Texas often falls near or above the national average due to its size, exposure to severe weather, and a growing rental market.

HOW_MUCH_LANDLORD.TITLE: How Much Landlord Insurance Do You Actually Need?
HOW_MUCH_LANDLORD.DESC1: When determining how much landlord insurance you need, start with the replacement cost of your rental property — not just its market value. Your dwelling coverage should be high enough to rebuild the home completely if it’s destroyed by a covered peril. Most landlord policies also include liability limits, which typically start at $300,000 and go up to $1 million or more per occurrence to protect you against lawsuits from injuries or accidents on your property. Higher liability limits or an umbrella policy can be wise if you own multiple properties or have significant personal assets at stake.
HOW_MUCH_LANDLORD.DESC2: Besides dwelling and liability coverage, you need enough coverage for lost rental income (fair rental value) if the property becomes uninhabitable, as well as coverage for landlord‑owned personal property like appliances. Insurance professionals often recommend matching coverage limits to your net worth and risk profile, since inadequate limits could expose you to out‑of‑pocket losses. Property value, local risks (like weather), and tenant type all factor into how much insurance you should carry — so getting multiple quotes helps ensure you have sufficient protection without unnecessary cost.

HEADER.TITLE: Factors That Impact Your Landlord Insurance Rates in Texas
HEADER.DESC: Several factors affect landlord insurance rates in Texas, including property location, age, and condition, as well as coverage limits and deductible amounts. Other influences include rental type, tenant history, claims history, local crime rates, natural disaster risk, and additional endorsements such as flood or earthquake coverage, all of which determine your premium.

LOCATION.TITLE: Location of Your Rental Property
LOCATION.DESC: The neighborhood and city of your rental property influence insurance premiums based on local risks and demand.

PROPERTY_AGE.TITLE: Age and Condition of the Property
PROPERTY_AGE.DESC: Older or poorly maintained properties may increase premiums due to a higher risk of damage or costly repairs.

PROPERTY_TYPE.TITLE: Type of Property (Single-Family vs. Multi-Family vs. Condo)
PROPERTY_TYPE.DESC: Insurance rates vary depending on whether the property is a single-family home, multi-unit building, or condo unit.

UNIT_COUNT.TITLE: Number of Units on the Property
UNIT_COUNT.DESC: More units typically increase risk exposure, leading to higher premiums compared to a single rental unit.

CONSTRUCTION.TITLE: Construction Material (Wood Frame vs. Brick vs. Concrete)
CONSTRUCTION.DESC: The building materials impact rates; brick or concrete usually lowers risk compared to wood-frame construction.

ROOF_CONDITION.TITLE: Roof Age and Condition
ROOF_CONDITION.DESC: An older or damaged roof can increase insurance costs due to a higher likelihood of leaks or storm damage.

COAST_PROXIMITY.TITLE: Proximity to the Coast or Flood Zones
COAST_PROXIMITY.DESC: Properties near the coast or in flood-prone areas face higher premiums due to increased natural-disaster risk.

WINDSTORM_RISK.TITLE: Windstorm and Hurricane Risk in Your Area
WINDSTORM_RISK.DESC: Areas with higher hurricane or windstorm exposure will see higher premiums to cover potential storm damage.

CRIME_RATE.TITLE: Crime Rate in Your Area
CRIME_RATE.DESC: Neighborhood crime rates affect liability and property coverage costs, with higher crime areas raising premiums.

FIRE_STATION_DISTANCE.TITLE: Distance to Nearest Fire Station
FIRE_STATION_DISTANCE.DESC: Properties farther from fire stations may face higher premiums due to slower emergency response times.

FIRE_FEATURES.TITLE: Fire Protection Features (Smoke Detectors, Sprinklers)
FIRE_FEATURES.DESC: Installing smoke alarms, sprinklers, and other fire safety features can significantly lower insurance rates.

SECURITY_FEATURES.TITLE: Security Features (Alarms, Cameras, Deadbolts)
SECURITY_FEATURES.DESC: Enhanced security measures, such as alarms, cameras, and strong locks, reduce risk and may lower your premiums.

COVERAGE_AMOUNT.TITLE: Coverage Amount You Choose
COVERAGE_AMOUNT.DESC: Higher coverage limits provide more protection but will increase premiums compared to lower coverage amounts.

DEDUCTIBLE.TITLE: Your Deductible Amount
DEDUCTIBLE.DESC: Choosing a higher deductible can lower premiums, while a lower deductible increases your insurance cost.

CLAIMS_HISTORY.TITLE: Your Claims History
CLAIMS_HISTORY.DESC: Past insurance claims for landlord insurance can impact your rates; frequent claims may result in higher premiums.

CREDIT_SCORE.TITLE: Your Credit Score
CREDIT_SCORE.DESC: A higher credit score can help lower landlord insurance rates, while lower scores may increase premiums.

TENANT_TYPE.TITLE: Type of Tenants (Long-Term vs. Short-Term)
TENANT_TYPE.DESC: Short-term or transient tenants may increase risk, leading to higher insurance rates than long-term tenants.

FURNISHED_STATUS.TITLE: Whether Property is Furnished or Unfurnished
FURNISHED_STATUS.DESC: Furnished rentals may increase premiums because more personal property is at risk of damage or theft.

OCCUPANCY_STATUS.TITLE: Whether Property is Vacant or Occupied
OCCUPANCY_STATUS.DESC: Vacant properties are higher risk for vandalism or undetected damage, often increasing insurance premiums.

PORTFOLIO_SIZE.TITLE: Number of Rental Properties You Own
PORTFOLIO_SIZE.DESC: Owning multiple rentals properties can affect rates, as insurers assess total exposure across all properties.

PET_POLICY.TITLE: Whether You Allow Pets on the Property
PET_POLICY.DESC: Allowing pets may slightly increase premiums due to potential damage to the rental property or liability claims.

SMOKING_POLICY.TITLE: Whether You Allow Smoking on the Property
SMOKING_POLICY.DESC: Smoking increases the risk of fire, which can result in higher insurance premiums for the rental property.

RENTAL_INCOME.TITLE: Rental Income Amount
RENTAL_INCOME.DESC: Higher rental income can influence rates because insurers calculate potential liability and replacement costs.

BUNDLING.TITLE: Bundling With Other Policies (Auto, Home, etc.)
BUNDLING.DESC: Bundling with landlord insurance with other policies can provide discounts and lower overall premiums.

CARRIER.TITLE: Insurance Carrier You Choose
CARRIER.DESC: Different carriers offer varying rates, discounts, and coverage options, affecting your total premium cost.

HEADER.TITLE: How to Maximize Your Discounts and Lower Your Premium
HEADER.DESC: Maximize your landlord insurance discounts in Texas by bundling policies, maintaining a secure property, installing fire and safety devices, and keeping a clean claims history. Higher deductibles, long-term tenant leases, and choosing qualified carriers can also lower premiums. Regularly reviewing coverage ensures you only pay for what you truly need, saving money while staying fully protected.

BUNDLING.TITLE: Multi-Policy / Bundling Discount
BUNDLING.DESC: Save by bundling landlord insurance with other policies, such as auto or home, to reduce your overall annual premiums.

MULTI_PROPERTY.TITLE: Multi-Property Portfolio Discount
MULTI_PROPERTY.DESC: Owning multiple rental properties may qualify you for discounts, as insurers reward larger portfolios with lower rates.

CLAIM_FREE.TITLE: Claims-Free Discount
CLAIM_FREE.DESC: Maintaining a history without insurance claims indicates low risk, helping you secure premium discounts.

LOYALTY.TITLE: Loyalty Discount
LOYALTY.DESC: Long-term policyholders often receive loyalty discounts for staying with the same insurance carrier over the years.

NEW_PROPERTY.TITLE: New Property Discount
NEW_PROPERTY.DESC: Newly purchased rental properties may qualify for a discount, as they are less likely to require immediate repairs.

NEW_ROOF.TITLE: New Roof Discount
NEW_ROOF.DESC: Installing a new roof reduces the risk of water damage, which lowers premiums through insurer discounts.

RENOVATED.TITLE: Recently Renovated Property Discount
RENOVATED.DESC: Recent renovations, like updated plumbing or electrical systems, can reduce risk and earn insurance discounts.

WIND_MITIGATION.TITLE: Wind Mitigation / Storm Shutters Discount
WIND_MITIGATION.DESC: Adding wind mitigation features or storm shutters can lower premiums in hurricane-prone areas.

SECURITY_SYSTEM.TITLE: Security System Discount
SECURITY_SYSTEM.DESC: A professionally monitored security system reduces the risk of theft, qualifying your rental property for premium discounts.

SMOKE_DETECTOR.TITLE: Smoke Detector and Fire Alarm Discount
SMOKE_DETECTOR.DESC: Installing smoke detectors and fire alarms helps prevent major damage, which can result in lower insurance rates.

SPRINKLER_SYSTEM.TITLE: Sprinkler System Discount
SPRINKLER_SYSTEM.DESC: Automatic sprinkler systems in your rental property reduce fire risk and can lower your insurance premiums.

DEADBOLT.TITLE: Deadbolt and Door Lock Discount
DEADBOLT.DESC: High-quality deadbolts and door locks enhance security, enabling insurers to offer discounted rates for lower risk.

GATED.TITLE: Gated Property Discount
GATED.DESC: A gated property increases security and decreases liability risk, which may lower landlord insurance premiums.

NON_SMOKER_POLICY.TITLE: Non-Smoker Policy Discount (No Smoking Allowed on Property)

HIGH_DEDUCTIBLE.TITLE: Higher Deductible Discount
HIGH_DEDUCTIBLE.DESC: Opting for a higher deductible reduces the insurer's risk and can lower your overall annual premium.

LONG_TERM_TENANT.TITLE: Long-Term Tenant Discount

TENANT_RENTERS_INSURANCE.TITLE: Tenant Renters Insurance Requirement Discount
TENANT_RENTERS_INSURANCE.DESC: Requiring tenants to carry renters insurance reduces risk and may result in landlord insurance discounts.

PROPERTY_MANAGEMENT.TITLE: Property Management Company Discount
PROPERTY_MANAGEMENT.DESC: Using a licensed property management company can reduce risk, qualifying your policy for lower premiums.

HOME_INSPECTION.TITLE: Home Inspection Discount
HOME_INSPECTION.DESC: Regular home inspections identify hazards early, helping you earn discounts by demonstrating proactive risk management.

PROXIMITY_DISCOUNT.TITLE: Primary Residence Nearby Discount (Landlord Lives Close to Property)
PROXIMITY_DISCOUNT.DESC: Living near your rental property allows a quick response to issues, lowering risk and qualifying for insurance discounts.

EXPERIENCED_LANDLORD.TITLE: Experienced Landlord Discount

WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.TITLE: What is Earthquake Insurance and Why Do You Need It?
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC1: Earthquake insurance is a type of protection designed to cover damage caused by ground movement, which is not typically included in standard home insurance policies. When an earthquake strikes, the cost of repairing structural damage or replacing damaged belongings can be overwhelming. This coverage helps reduce that financial burden by offering support when it matters most.
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC2: Even in areas where earthquakes are not frequent, the risk still exists, and the impact can be severe. Having the right coverage in place means you are not left handling unexpected expenses alone. It provides reassurance that your home, belongings, and stability are protected during uncertain situations.

LIST.TITLE: Coverage for Structural Damage
LIST.TEXT: Covers major damage to your home’s structure, including walls, roof, and foundation, helping you manage expensive repairs after unexpected ground movement or sudden seismic events.

LIST.TITLE: Protection for Personal Belongings
LIST.TEXT: Helps replace or repair furniture, electronics, and everyday items damaged during an earthquake, so you can recover faster without worrying about replacing essential belongings out of pocket.

LIST.TITLE: Additional Living Expenses
LIST.TEXT: Supports temporary housing, food, and basic living costs if your home becomes unsafe to live in, ensuring your daily life continues with less disruption during repairs.

LIST.TITLE: Not Included in Standard Policies
LIST.TEXT: Explains that regular home insurance policies usually do not include earthquake damage, making separate coverage important for anyone who wants complete and reliable protection.

LIST.TITLE: Peace of Mind for the Unexpected
LIST.TEXT: Offers confidence and financial security, knowing you are prepared for rare but serious events that could otherwise create long-term stress and costly repairs.

EARTHQUAKE_REQUIRED.TITLE: Is Earthquake Insurance Required in Texas?
EARTHQUAKE_REQUIRED.DESC1: Earthquake insurance is not required in Texas by law, and most standard landlord or homeowners insurance policies do not include earthquake coverage. While earthquakes are less common in Texas compared to states like California, minor seismic activity has been recorded in certain regions, making it a consideration for some property owners.
EARTHQUAKE_REQUIRED.DESC2: Because it’s not mandatory, the decision to purchase earthquake insurance depends on your property’s location, structure, and overall risk tolerance. Areas with increased seismic activity or properties built on certain soil types may face a higher risk of damage, a risk that standard policies typically exclude. If you want protection against earthquake-related losses, you can add a separate earthquake policy or endorsement to your landlord insurance. This coverage can help pay for structural repairs, rebuilding costs, and sometimes loss of rental income, giving you added financial security and peace of mind.

HOMEOWNERS_VS_EARTHQUAKE.TITLE: Does My Homeowners Insurance Cover Earthquake Damage?
HOMEOWNERS_VS_EARTHQUAKE.DESC1: In most cases, standard homeowners' insurance does not cover damage caused by earthquakes. While it typically protects against risks like fire, theft, or storms, seismic activity is usually excluded. This means if an earthquake damages your home’s structure or belongings, you would likely have to cover those repair and replacement costs on your own.
HOMEOWNERS_VS_EARTHQUAKE.DESC2: To be protected, you usually need to purchase a separate earthquake insurance policy or add it as an endorsement, depending on what options are available. This extra coverage helps fill the gap left by standard policies, ensuring your home and finances are better protected if unexpected ground movement occurs.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Earthquake Insurance Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Earthquake insurance typically covers damage to your home’s structure, including the foundation, walls, ceilings, and roof, caused by sudden ground movement. It can also help repair or replace personal belongings such as furniture, appliances, and electronics. Many policies include coverage for additional living expenses, helping pay for temporary housing if your home becomes unsafe after an earthquake.

STANDARD.TITLE: Standard Coverages (Included in Most Policies)
STANDARD.DESC: Most earthquake insurance policies include essential protections that cover the structure, foundation, personal property, and additional living expenses.

LIST.TITLE: Dwelling Coverage (The Structure of Your Home)
LIST.DESC: Covers the main structure of your home, including the roof, walls, and built-in systems. If an earthquake causes damage, this coverage helps pay for repairs or rebuilding, so your home can be restored safely without full out-of-pocket costs.

LIST.TITLE: Foundation Damage
LIST.DESC: Protects against cracks, shifting, or weakening of your home’s foundation caused by seismic movement. Since foundation issues can affect the entire structure, this coverage helps cover the expensive repairs needed to stabilize and secure your home.

LIST.TITLE: Chimney and Fireplace Damage
LIST.DESC: Helps cover repair or rebuilding costs if your chimney or fireplace cracks, tilts, or collapses during an earthquake. These structures are highly vulnerable, making this coverage important for both safety and the restoration of proper function.

LIST.TITLE: Walls, Ceilings, and Floors
LIST.DESC: Provides coverage for damage to interior and exterior surfaces, including cracks, separation, or collapse. Earthquake vibrations can weaken these areas, and this protection helps restore your home’s structure and livability after damage occurs.

LIST.TITLE: Attached Structures (Garages, Carports)
LIST.DESC: Covers structures connected to your home, such as garages and carports, if damaged by seismic activity. This ensures that repairs or rebuilding costs are included, helping to maintain the full functionality and value of your property.

LIST.TITLE: Other Structures (Fences, Sheds, Driveways)
LIST.DESC: Extends coverage to detached structures like fences, sheds, and driveways. Earthquakes can cause cracks or collapse, and this protection helps cover repair costs so your entire property, not just your home, is restored properly.

LIST.TITLE: Personal Property / Contents Coverage
LIST.DESC: Helps repair or replace personal belongings damaged during an earthquake. This includes everyday household items, reducing the financial burden of replacing essential possessions after unexpected structural or interior damage.

LIST.TITLE: Clothing and Furniture
LIST.DESC: Covers damage to clothing and furniture, beds, sofas, and other furniture affected by earthquake movement. If items are broken or destroyed, this coverage helps you replace them quickly so your daily routine can return to normal.

LIST.TITLE: Electronics and Appliances
LIST.DESC: Protects electronics and appliances such as TVs, laptops, refrigerators, and kitchen appliances. Earthquake shaking can cause internal damage or breakage, and this coverage helps cover repair or replacement costs for essential home equipment.

LIST.TITLE: Valuable Items (Up to Policy Limits)
LIST.DESC: Provides limited protection for valuable goods like jewelry, collectibles, and artwork. While coverage is capped, it still offers financial support if these items are damaged or lost due to earthquake-related incidents.

LIST.TITLE: Loss of Use / Additional Living Expenses
LIST.DESC: Helps cover extra costs and additional living expenses if your home becomes unlivable after an earthquake. This includes temporary housing, food, and daily living expenses, allowing you to maintain stability while your home is repaired or rebuilt.

LIST.TITLE: Temporary Housing and Hotel Costs
LIST.DESC: Temporary housing pays for hotel stays or short-term rentals if your home is unsafe to live in. This ensures you and your family have a secure place to stay without worrying about immediate accommodation expenses after damage occurs.

LIST.TITLE: Building Code Upgrade Coverage (Ordinance or Law)
LIST.DESC: Covers all additional costs required to bring your home up to current building codes during earthquake repairs. If regulations have changed, this coverage ensures necessary upgrades are completed beyond standard structural restoration work.

LIST.TITLE: Emergency Repairs Coverage
LIST.DESC: Helps pay for urgent repairs immediately after an earthquake to prevent further damage. This can include temporary stabilization, boarding up damaged areas, and quick fixes while waiting for complete restoration to safely repair your home.

LIST.TITLE: Debris Removal Coverage
LIST.DESC: Covers the cost of removing all debris caused by earthquake damage, including broken structures, materials, and rubble. Cleanup is necessary before any repair work can begin, and this coverage ensures these expenses are handled.

LIST.TITLE: Masonry and Brick Veneer Damage
LIST.DESC: Provides protection for damage to exterior brickwork, stone, or veneer caused by earthquake activity. Cracks or collapses can be expensive to repair, and this coverage ensures proper rebuilding and stabilization of your home’s exterior surfaces.

LIST.TITLE: Swimming Pool and Spa Damage
LIST.DESC: Covers damage to swimming pools, spas, or hot tubs caused by earthquakes, including structural cracks, leaks, or foundation shifts. This coverage helps manage the high cost of repairs so features can be safely restored without extra financial burden.

LIST.TITLE: Retaining Wall Damage
LIST.DESC: Helps cover repair costs for retaining walls that support soil, landscaping, or property features. Earthquakes can weaken or collapse these structures, and this coverage ensures walls are rebuilt or stabilized to prevent further property damage.

LIST.TITLE: Land Stabilization Coverage
LIST.DESC: Provides coverage for stabilizing land affected by seismic shifts, including work to prevent further movement, erosion, or soil sinking. This ensures your home’s foundation and surrounding property remain secure after an earthquake event.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Earthquake Insurance NOT Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Earthquake insurance in Texas typically does not cover damage caused by flooding, landslides, or mudslides that may accompany seismic activity. It also usually excludes normal wear and tear, maintenance issues, and damage from mold, pests, and gradual structural problems unrelated to sudden earthquakes. Homeowners should review their policy carefully to understand what is excluded.

FLOOD_AFTER_EARTHQUAKE.TITLE: Flood Damage Caused by Earthquake (Tsunami, Overflow)
FLOOD_AFTER_EARTHQUAKE.DESC: Earthquake insurance generally does not cover flooding, tsunamis, or water overflow caused by seismic activity. Any damage from rising water, river overflow, or coastal surges will usually require separate flood coverage to repair or replace.

FIRE_AFTER_EARTHQUAKE.TITLE: Fire Damage Following an Earthquake (Separate Homeowners Claim)
FIRE_AFTER_EARTHQUAKE.DESC: Damage from fire that occurs after an earthquake is typically not covered under earthquake insurance. Homeowners may need to file a separate claim under their standard homeowners policy to address fire-related losses or rebuilding costs.

VEHICLES.TITLE: Vehicles and Other Self-Propelled Vehicles
VEHICLES.DESC: Earthquake policies usually do not cover cars, motorcycles, RVs, or other self-propelled vehicles. Damage to vehicles during seismic events requires separate auto insurance, as earthquake insurance focuses on buildings and personal property.

LANDSCAPING.TITLE: Landscaping, Trees, Plants, and Shrubs
LANDSCAPING.DESC: Damage to outdoor landscaping, including trees, shrubs, plants, and flower beds, is generally excluded. Earthquake insurance focuses on structures and personal property inside the home, so replacing damaged landscaping requires additional coverage.

WEAR_TEAR.TITLE: Wear and Tear / General Maintenance
WEAR_TEAR.DESC: Normal wear and tear or general maintenance issues, even if worsened by seismic activity, are not covered. Earthquake insurance only protects against sudden and accidental damage caused directly by an earthquake, not gradual deterioration or neglect.

PRE_EXISTING_DAMAGE.TITLE: Pre-Existing Structural Damage
PRE_EXISTING_DAMAGE.DESC: Damage that existed before the earthquake is not covered. Policies typically require the property to be in good condition at the time of purchase, so repairs are needed for prior cracks, foundation issues, or structural weaknesses.

MOLD_MILDEW.TITLE: Mold and Mildew Following Earthquake Damage
MOLD_MILDEW.DESC: Mold, mildew, or fungal growth resulting from earthquake damage is generally not included. While structural repairs may be covered, secondary issues like mold cleanup require separate coverage or must be addressed by the homeowner independently.

BUSINESS_INTERRUPTION.TITLE: Business Interruption Losses (Residential Policies)
BUSINESS_INTERRUPTION.DESC: Earthquake insurance for homes does not typically cover losses related to running a business from home. Any income lost due to property damage or operational downtime will not be reimbursed unless a separate commercial policy is purchased.

CURRENCY_VALUABLES.TITLE: Currency, Precious Metals, and Valuable Papers
CURRENCY_VALUABLES.DESC: Cash, coins, bullion, important documents, or collectibles like stocks and bonds are often excluded. Earthquake insurance covers physical property and belongings inside the home, so these items may need separate protection or safekeeping.

POOLS_SPAS.TITLE: Swimming Pools and Hot Tubs (in most cases)
POOLS_SPAS.DESC: Most earthquake insurance policies do not cover damage to pools, hot tubs, or spas. Structural cracks, leaks, or shifting caused by earthquakes are usually excluded unless specifically added to the policy through an endorsement or separate coverage.

FENCES_WALLS.TITLE: Fences, Retaining Walls, and Seawalls (in most cases)
FENCES_WALLS.DESC: Damage to fences, retaining walls, or seawalls is commonly not covered under standard earthquake policies. Unless added as an endorsement, homeowners must pay out of pocket for repairs to these outdoor structures affected by seismic activity.

BELOW_DEDUCTIBLE.TITLE: Damage Below the Deductible (Typically 10–25% of Dwelling Value)
BELOW_DEDUCTIBLE.DESC: Any damage that falls below the policy’s earthquake deductible is not reimbursed. Deductibles typically range from 10–25% of the dwelling’s value, meaning minor cracks or small-scale damage will not trigger a payout under most policies.

GROUND_SETTLEMENT.TITLE: Gradual Ground Settlement and Soil Erosion
GROUND_SETTLEMENT.DESC: Slow-moving land shifts, soil erosion, or ground settling over time are generally excluded. Earthquake insurance is designed to cover sudden, accidental damage caused by seismic activity, not environmental changes that occur over time.

SINKHOLES.TITLE: Sinkholes (Unless Added as Endorsement)
SINKHOLES.DESC: Sinkhole formation is usually not covered unless specifically added through an endorsement. If your home is damaged by a natural sinkhole, repairs or stabilization work will not be included under standard earthquake coverage.

GOVERNMENT_SEIZURE.TITLE: Government Seizure or Demolition
GOVERNMENT_SEIZURE.DESC: Earthquake insurance does not cover losses resulting from government seizure or demolition, including property seizure, condemnation, or demolition. Any damage or loss due to a legal or regulatory authority must be addressed outside the policy.

WAR_NUCLEAR.TITLE: Nuclear Hazard or War
WAR_NUCLEAR.DESC: Damage caused by nuclear hazards, war, or acts of terrorism is not covered. Earthquake insurance only addresses natural seismic events, so any man-made disasters or radioactive contamination require separate specialized coverage.

INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE.TITLE: Intentional Damage
INTENTIONAL_DAMAGE.DESC: Deliberate or intentional damage acts that cause extreme property damage are excluded from earthquake insurance. Coverage is only for accidental and sudden damage caused by natural seismic events, not harm caused by human actions.

WAITING_PERIOD.TITLE: Losses Occurring Before the Waiting Period Ends
WAITING_PERIOD.DESC: Most earthquake insurance policies include a waiting period before coverage becomes active. Any damage or loss occurring during this initial period is excluded from coverage, meaning claims for incidents before the policy takes effect are excluded.

INDUCED_SEISMICITY_EXCLUSION.TITLE: Damage from Induced Seismicity (in some policies)
INDUCED_SEISMICITY_EXCLUSION.DESC: Earthquake damage caused by human activities, such as fracking or other industrial actions, is often excluded. Policies generally cover only natural seismic events, so damage from induced seismicity may require additional or specialized insurance.

DETACHED_STRUCTURES.TITLE: Detached Structures (Unless Specifically Added)
DETACHED_STRUCTURES.DESC: Detached structures, including guest houses, garages, sheds, or barns, are usually not covered unless specifically added via endorsement. Earthquake insurance primarily protects the primary home and its contents, excluding other buildings.

COST.TITLE: How Much Does Earthquake Insurance Cost in Texas?
COST.DESC1: Earthquake insurance in Texas is typically more affordable than in high‑risk states. According to TexasInsurance.org, premiums can range from about $500 to $800 per year for a residential property, depending on coverage limits, deductible levels, and risk factors such as location and building age. This means many Texas homeowners pay several hundred dollars annually for earthquake protection, though exact rates vary by insurer and specific home details.
COST.DESC2: When compared with other states, Texas generally has lower earthquake insurance costs because it’s considered a lower‑risk area for seismic activity. States with frequent and stronger earthquakes, such as California or Alaska, often see average annual premiums of $800 to $2,000 or more, reflecting higher expected losses from quakes. This regional difference highlights how earthquake risk influences insurance pricing across the U.S., making Texas comparatively less expensive to insure against seismic damage.

HOW_MUCH_EARTHQUAKE.TITLE: How Much Earthquake Insurance Do You Actually Need?
HOW_MUCH_EARTHQUAKE.DESC1: When deciding how much earthquake insurance you need, experts recommend that your dwelling coverage should at least match the amount it would cost to fully rebuild your home if it were completely destroyed by a quake. For instance, if your homeowners' policy has $500,000 in dwelling coverage, then your earthquake coverage should be at least $500,000 or more, because you can’t choose a lower limit and still be fully protected. This ensures you have enough funds to rebuild your house to a similar standard, without being underinsured when disaster strikes.
HOW_MUCH_EARTHQUAKE.DESC2: In addition to dwelling coverage, it’s important to consider personal property limits and additional living expenses so you’re covered for belongings and temporary housing if your home becomes uninhabitable. Many insurers allow you to raise these limits based on your needs, and having enough coverage for both rebuilding costs and living expenses can make recovery smoother and less financially stressful after an earthquake.

HEADER.TITLE: Factors That Impact Your Earthquake Insurance Rates in Texas
HEADER.DESC: Several factors influence earthquake insurance rates in Texas. Key elements include your home's location, construction type, age, and foundation design. The value of your dwelling and personal property, chosen coverage limits, deductible amount, and proximity to fault lines also affect premiums. Insurance companies assess these risks carefully to determine your annual cost.

LOCATION.TITLE: Location of Your Property
LOCATION.DESC: Your home’s location directly impacts earthquake insurance premiums based on local seismic risk.

FAULT_PROXIMITY.TITLE: Proximity to Fault Lines
FAULT_PROXIMITY.DESC: Being near an active fault line increases earthquake risk, raising insurance premiums for your property coverage.

OIL_GAS_PROXIMITY.TITLE: Proximity to Oil and Gas Operations
OIL_GAS_PROXIMITY.DESC: Homes near fracking or drilling sites face a higher risk of induced earthquakes, which can increase insurance costs.

INDUCED_RISK.TITLE: Induced Seismicity Risk in Your Area
INDUCED_RISK.DESC: Human-caused seismic activity, like drilling or fracking, affects your home’s earthquake insurance rate significantly.

SEISMIC_ZONE.TITLE: Seismic Zone Designation of Your Area
SEISMIC_ZONE.DESC: Homes in higher seismic zones face a greater risk of damage from earthquakes, making insurance rates higher than in lower-risk zones.

HOME_AGE.TITLE: Age and Condition of Your Home
HOME_AGE.DESC: Older or poorly maintained homes are more vulnerable to earthquake damage, which can raise coverage premiums.

CONSTRUCTION_TYPE.TITLE: Type of Construction (Wood Frame vs. Brick vs. Concrete)
CONSTRUCTION_TYPE.DESC: Brick- or concrete-type homes often cost more to insure against earthquakes than wood-framed structures.

FOUNDATION_TYPE.TITLE: Foundation Type (Slab, Crawlspace, Basement, Pier and Beam)
FOUNDATION_TYPE.DESC: Different foundation types react differently during quakes, affecting insurance costs for your home coverage.

STORIES.TITLE: Number of Stories in Your Home
STORIES.DESC: Multi-story homes may experience more structural stress in earthquakes, increasing your insurance rates.

SOIL_TYPE.TITLE: Soil Type Under Your Property
SOIL_TYPE.DESC: Soft or unstable soil beneath your property can amplify earthquake damage, leading insurers to charge higher premiums.

ROOF_CONDITION.TITLE: Roof Type and Condition
ROOF_CONDITION.DESC: Roof materials and condition affect vulnerability during a quake and influence your insurance premium.

CHIMNEY_PRESENCE.TITLE: Chimney and Fireplace Presence
CHIMNEY_PRESENCE.DESC: Chimneys or fireplaces can easily be damaged in quakes, which may increase your earthquake insurance cost.

COVERAGE_AMOUNT.TITLE: Coverage Amount You Choose
COVERAGE_AMOUNT.DESC: Higher dwelling coverage limits raise premiums, while lower limits reduce costs but may underinsure your home.

DEDUCTIBLE.TITLE: Your Deductible Amount (Typically 10–25% of Dwelling Value)
DEDUCTIBLE.DESC: Selecting a higher deductible lowers premiums, but increases out-of-pocket costs if earthquake damage occurs.

PERSONAL_PROPERTY_LIMIT.TITLE: Personal Property Coverage Amount
PERSONAL_PROPERTY_LIMIT.DESC: The value of personal belongings insured affects premiums; higher coverage limits increase policy costs.

LOSS_OF_USE_LIMIT.TITLE: Loss of Use Coverage Amount
LOSS_OF_USE_LIMIT.DESC: Coverage for temporary housing increases premiums based on the dollar amount chosen for this protection.

CLAIMS_HISTORY.TITLE: Your Claims History
CLAIMS_HISTORY.DESC: Frequent past claims signal a higher risk to insurers, potentially raising your earthquake insurance premium.

CREDIT_SCORE.TITLE: Your Credit Score
CREDIT_SCORE.DESC: Higher credit scores may help lower earthquake insurance premiums, while lower scores can raise rates.

PLUMBING_AGE.TITLE: Age and Condition of Your Plumbing and Electrical Systems
PLUMBING_AGE.DESC: Older plumbing or electrical systems increase the risk of damage, which can raise earthquake insurance costs.

SEISMIC_RETROFIT.TITLE: Whether Your Home Has Been Seismically Retrofitted
SEISMIC_RETROFIT.DESC: Seismic retrofitting strengthens your home and can lower insurance premiums by reducing earthquake risk.

FOUNDATION_BOLTED.TITLE: Whether Your Home is Bolted to Its Foundation
FOUNDATION_BOLTED.DESC: Homes securely bolted to foundations are more stable and can result in lower earthquake insurance premiums.

UTILITIES_SECURED.TITLE: Whether Utilities Are Strapped and Secured
UTILITIES_SECURED.DESC: Properly secured utility items reduce the risk of damage during quakes, helping lower insurance costs.

RESIDENCY_TYPE.TITLE: Whether Your Property is a Primary or Secondary Residence
RESIDENCY_TYPE.DESC: Secondary homes or vacation properties typically incur higher insurance premiums than primary residences.

BUNDLING.TITLE: Bundling With Other Policies (Auto, Home, Flood, etc.)
BUNDLING.DESC: Combining earthquake insurance with other policies may qualify you for discounts, reducing your total premium.

CARRIER.TITLE: Insurance Carrier You Choose
CARRIER.DESC: Different insurers assess earthquake risk differently, resulting in significant premium variations among carriers.

HEADER.TITLE: How to Maximize Your Discounts and Lower Your Premium
HEADER.DESC: Earthquake insurance can be expensive, but there are many strategies to reduce your premium while maintaining strong coverage. Understanding the factors that influence your rates and actively managing significant savings. Insurers consider home characteristics, risk mitigation measures, and policy when calculating premiums. By taking proactive steps, homeowners can make coverage more affordable.

SEISMIC_RETROFIT.TITLE: Seismic Retrofit Discount
SEISMIC_RETROFIT.DESC: Homes that undergo comprehensive seismic retrofitting qualify for premium reductions due to reduced damage risk.

FOUNDATION_BOLTING.TITLE: Foundation Bolting Discount
FOUNDATION_BOLTING.DESC: Bolting your home securely to its foundation strengthens stability and helps lower earthquake insurance premiums.

CRIPPLE_WALL.TITLE: Cripple Wall Bracing Discount
CRIPPLE_WALL.DESC: Properly braced cripple walls improve earthquake resilience, which can effectively reduce your insurance costs.

SOFT_STORY.TITLE: Soft-Story Retrofitting Discount
SOFT_STORY.DESC: Soft-story retrofitting reduces the risk of collapse during earthquakes, allowing insurers to offer lower premiums.

WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.TITLE: What is Flood Insurance and Why Do You Need It?
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC: Flood insurance is a type of coverage that helps protect homeowners, renters, and businesses from financial loss due to flooding. Unlike standard homeowners' insurance, which typically doesn't cover flood-related damage, flood insurance offers specific protection for damages caused by water accumulation during floods. This can include both structural and personal property damage. Flood insurance policies are available through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and private insurers, giving you various options for coverage in case disaster strikes.
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.SUB_TITLE: The following are the reasons you need flood insurance:

LIST.TITLE: Floods Can Happen Anywhere
LIST.TEXT: Flooding isn't limited to areas near rivers or coastlines. Heavy rain, melting snow, or even broken plumbing can cause flooding in any region. Having flood insurance ensures you're protected, regardlesWhat is Flood Insurance and Why Do You Need It?s of your location.

LIST.TITLE: Your Homeowners Insurance Won't Cover Flood Damage
LIST.TEXT: Most traditional homeowners' insurance policies don't cover flood damage, which leaves you vulnerable in the event of a flood. Homeowners often face high flood risks, especially in flood-prone areas, so having a separate flood insurance policy is crucial.

LIST.TITLE: Federal Aid Might Not Be Enough
LIST.TEXT: In the aftermath of a flood, federal disaster assistance may not be sufficient to fully recover from the damage. Flood insurance helps fill the gap, offering you more coverage for repairs and replacement of personal property than government aid can provide.

LIST.TITLE: Protect Your Home's Structure
LIST.TEXT: Flood insurance helps cover structural repairs to your home. This includes damage to walls, the foundation, plumbing, electrical systems, and HVAC, all of which are critical to restoring your home to a livable condition.

LIST.TITLE: Protect Valuable Personal Property
LIST.TEXT: Flood insurance also covers personal property, including furniture, electronics, and clothing. This can be a financial lifesaver in the event of a flood, as replacing these items can be costly without coverage.

FLOOD_REQUIRED.TITLE: Is Flood Insurance Required in Texas?
FLOOD_REQUIRED.DESC1: In Texas, flood insurance is not mandatory for all homeowners. However, if your property is located in a high-risk flood zone, as determined by FEMA's flood maps, and you have a federally-backed mortgage, flood insurance is required. Lenders will often require flood insurance as a condition of the loan to protect their investment, especially in areas with a history of frequent flooding.
FLOOD_REQUIRED.DESC2: Even if you're not in a high-risk flood zone, it's still wise to consider flood insurance. Many Texans live in moderate or low-risk zones, but flooding can still occur unexpectedly. In fact, over 20% of flood claims come from properties that aren't considered high-risk. Choosing to purchase flood insurance in these cases can provide extra peace of mind, especially as extreme weather events become more frequent in the state.

HOMEOWNERS_VS_FLOOD.TITLE: Does My Homeowners Insurance Cover Flood Damage?
HOMEOWNERS_VS_FLOOD.DESC1: No, homeowners' insurance typically does not cover flood damage. While it protects your property from common perils like fire, theft, and certain types of water damage (such as burst pipes), flooding is usually excluded from standard policies. This means that if a flood occurs, your homeowners' insurance won't cover the costs of repairing your home or replacing personal belongings damaged by floodwaters.
HOMEOWNERS_VS_FLOOD.DESC2: To protect your home and personal property from flood damage, you will need to purchase a separate flood insurance policy. This specialized coverage is available through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) or private insurers. It's essential for homeowners in Texas to consider flood insurance, as the state is prone to heavy rain, hurricanes, and rising water, which can lead to significant flood-related damage.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Flood Insurance Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Flood insurance in Texas typically covers both the structure of your home and personal property. This includes the building's foundation, plumbing, electrical systems, and HVAC. It also protects personal items like clothing, furniture, electronics, and appliances. Additionally, flood insurance can cover debris removal and flood mitigation measures, ensuring you're well-prepared after a flood.

STANDARD.TITLE: Standard Coverages (Included in Most Policies)
STANDARD.DESC: Most flood insurance policies include essential protections that cover the building structure, foundation, electrical systems, personal property, and debris removal.

LIST.TITLE: Building / Dwelling Coverage
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance covers your home's structure, ensuring repairs are made to the dwelling itself. This includes the walls, roof, and foundation, providing crucial protection when floodwaters compromise your home's integrity.

LIST.TITLE: Foundation and Structural Elements
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance covers damage to the foundation and key structural elements, such as beams, columns, and walls. It ensures that your home's framework is restored to its original condition after a flood, preventing costly repairs.

LIST.TITLE: Electrical and Plumbing Systems
LIST.DESC: The electrical and plumbing systems in your home are covered under flood insurance. This includes wiring, outlets, switches, and plumbing pipes. If these systems are damaged by floodwaters, insurance will cover the cost of repairs and replacements.

LIST.TITLE: HVAC Systems (Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning)
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance also covers HVAC systems, which are damaged by floodwaters. This includes air conditioning, heating systems, and ventilation units. Replacing or repairing these systems can be costly, but flood insurance provides the protection.

LIST.TITLE: Water Heaters and Built-In Appliances
LIST.DESC: Your water heater and built-in appliances, such as dishwashers, stoves, and refrigerators, are covered by flood insurance. These items can be expensive to repair or replace, so coverage helps protect against the financial burden of water damage.

LIST.TITLE: Permanently Installed Carpeting and Flooring
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance covers permanently installed carpeting and flooring in your home. Whether it's hardwood, tile, or carpet, this protection helps cover the cost of replacing flooring that's been ruined by floodwaters.

LIST.TITLE: Permanently Installed Cabinets and Paneling
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance covers the cost of replacing permanently installed cabinets, paneling, and other built-in features. These elements are often integral to the home's design, and their repair or replacement can be expensive without the right coverage.

LIST.TITLE: Window Blinds and Curtains
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance also covers window blinds, curtains, and other window treatments. If floodwaters damage these items, your insurance policy will help you replace them, ensuring that your home is restored to its pre-flood condition.

LIST.TITLE: Detached Garages
LIST.DESC: If your home has a detached garage, flood insurance will cover repairs to this structure. This includes damage to the garage's walls, roof, and foundation, as well as items stored within, such as tools or vehicles (depending on the policy).

LIST.TITLE: Personal Property / Contents Coverage
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance also covers personal property, including household items like furniture, clothing, and electronics. This insurance coverage is designed to replace valuable possessions that may be destroyed or damaged by floodwaters.

LIST.TITLE: Clothing and Furniture
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance helps cover the cost of replacing clothing and furniture that is damaged by floodwaters. Personal items, especially those with sentimental value, can be costly to replace, making flood insurance a vital tool in safeguarding you.

LIST.TITLE: Electronics and Appliances
LIST.DESC: Your electronics, including TVs, computers, and kitchen appliances, are covered under flood insurance. This protection ensures that if your electronics are damaged by a flood, you'll receive financial compensation for repair or replacement.

LIST.TITLE: Curtains and Portable Air Conditioners
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance includes coverage for curtains and portable air conditioners. These items are often damaged during a flood, and the insurance policy ensures you'll be reimbursed for their repair or replacement, helping restore comfort to your home.

LIST.TITLE: Valuable Items (Up to Policy Limits)
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance covers valuable items, such as original artwork, furs, and jewelry, up to policy limits. This allows you to protect prized possessions in the event of flood-related damage, ensuring they're replaced or restored.

LIST.TITLE: Washing Machines and Dryers
LIST.DESC: Your washing machine and dryer are covered under flood insurance. These appliances are often vulnerable to water damage during a flood, but with the right coverage, you can have them repaired or replaced without bearing the full financial burden.

LIST.TITLE: Food Freezers and the Food Inside
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance covers damage to food freezers and the food stored inside. If floodwaters cause your freezer to malfunction or be destroyed, your insurance policy can help cover the cost of replacing the appliance and the food inside.

LIST.TITLE: Original Artwork and Furs (Up to Policy Limits)
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance offers protection for valuable items such as original artwork and furs, within the policy's coverage limits. If these items are damaged during a flood, your insurance will help cover the cost of restoring or replacing them.

LIST.TITLE: Debris Removal Coverage
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance provides debris removal coverage, helping to cover the cost of removing debris left behind after a flood. This can include the cost of removing destroyed items or clearing up the damage, ensuring your property is ready for repairs.

LIST.TITLE: Loss Avoidance Measures (Sandbags, Pumps)
LIST.DESC: Flood insurance includes coverage for loss-avoidance measures, such as sandbags and pumps, used to prevent flood damage. If these measures are necessary to protect your home, your policy will cover the cost of these preventative actions.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Flood Insurance NOT Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Flood insurance in Texas has certain exclusions. It doesn't cover damage caused by moisture, mold, or mildew unless it's directly caused by the flood. It also doesn't cover items outside the insured building, such as landscaping, fences, or vehicles. Additionally, it doesn't include financial losses like lost wages or temporary housing costs, which are often excluded from flood policies.

MOISTURE_MOLD.TITLE: Damage Caused by Moisture, Mildew, or Mold (Preventable by Owner)
MOISTURE_MOLD.DESC: Flood insurance doesn't cover damage caused by moisture, mildew, or mold that could have been prevented by proper maintenance. Homeowners must take steps to prevent mold growth, as policies typically exclude damages arising from failure to mitigate.

CURRENCY_VALUABLES.TITLE: Currency, Precious Metals, and Valuable Papers
CURRENCY_VALUABLES.DESC: Flood insurance excludes coverage for currency, precious metals, or valuable papers like deeds, bonds, or stock certificates. These items are considered high-risk and should be stored securely in safes or off-site to prevent financial loss.

OUTDOOR_PROPERTY.TITLE: Property and Belongings Outside the Insured Building
OUTDOOR_PROPERTY.DESC: Items stored outside the insured building, such as outdoor furniture and other property in the yard, are not covered by flood insurance. Only the property inside the structure is protected, so outdoor possessions should be moved to safer locations.

LIVING_EXPENSES.TITLE: Living Expenses / Additional Living Expenses (ALE)
LIVING_EXPENSES.DESC: Flood insurance doesn't cover living expenses or temporary housing costs that arise if you have to evacuate your home. While some policies may include limited coverage, additional living expenses are excluded from most flood insurance plans.

BUSINESS_INTERRUPTION.TITLE: Business Interruption Losses
BUSINESS_INTERRUPTION.DESC: Flood insurance does not cover the loss of income or business interruptions caused by flooding. If your business is affected, you may need a separate commercial flood policy or business interruption coverage to protect against this financial loss.

VEHICLES.TITLE: Vehicles and Other Self-Propelled Vehicles
VEHICLES.DESC: Flood insurance policies do not cover vehicles, boats, or other self-propelled vehicles. These items must be insured under a separate auto or vehicle insurance policy. Damage to vehicles caused by flooding is typically handled through auto insurance.

LANDSCAPING.TITLE: Landscaping, Trees, Plants, and Shrubs
LANDSCAPING.DESC: Flood insurance excludes coverage for landscaping, trees, plants, or shrubs. While a flood may damage your yard, it is considered exterior property and is not covered. Homeowners should consider landscaping insurance for these risks.

DECKS_PATIOS.TITLE: Decks, Patios, and Swimming Pools
DECKS_PATIOS.DESC: Damage to decks, patios, and swimming pools caused by flooding is not covered under standard flood insurance policies. These outdoor features are often excluded, so homeowners should consider separate insurance coverage for these areas.

FENCES_WALLS.TITLE: Fences, Retaining Walls, and Seawalls
FENCES_WALLS.DESC: Flood insurance does not cover fences, retaining walls, or seawalls. These are considered external features and are generally excluded. Property owners may need separate coverage or policies to protect these structures against flood damage.

SEPTIC_SYSTEMS.TITLE: Septic Systems and Well Water Tanks
SEPTIC_SYSTEMS.DESC: Septic systems and well water tanks are not covered by flood insurance. If these systems are damaged during a flood, homeowners will seek alternative coverage or bear the cost of repairs themselves, as flood policies exclude such damage.

FINANCIAL_LOSSES.TITLE: Financial Losses Caused by Flooding (Lost Wages, etc.)
FINANCIAL_LOSSES.DESC: Flood insurance does not cover financial losses such as lost wages or business income resulting from flooding. While property damage is covered, personal or business-related financial setbacks from being unable to work are excluded from standard flood policies.

SEWER_BACKUP.TITLE: Damage from Sewer Backup (Unless Caused Directly by Flooding)
SEWER_BACKUP.DESC: Sewer backup damage is generally not covered by flood insurance, unless it is caused directly by flooding. If the water backup occurs due to issues like a clogged drain or other non-flood causes, additional coverage would be needed.

EARTHQUAKE_LANDSLIDE.TITLE: Earthquake or Landslide Damage
EARTHQUAKE_LANDSLIDE.DESC: Flood insurance does not cover damage from natural disasters like earthquakes or landslides. These events are typically covered under separate insurance policies, such as earthquake or landslide coverage, which must be purchased independently.

GRADUAL_WATER.TITLE: Gradual Water Damage and Seepage
GRADUAL_WATER.DESC: Flood insurance does not cover gradual water damage or seepage that happens over time. For instance, leaks or slow infiltration of water through cracks in the foundation are excluded, as flood policies cover sudden, catastrophic flooding events.

TEMPORARY_HOUSING.TITLE: Temporary Housing and Hotel Costs
TEMPORARY_HOUSING.DESC: Flood insurance typically does not cover the costs of temporary housing or hotel stays. If your home becomes uninhabitable after a flood, you may need to rely on other types of insurance or assistance for living expenses while your home is repaired.

UNDERGROUND_STRUCTURES.TITLE: Underground Structures and Pipelines
UNDERGROUND_STRUCTURES.DESC: Underground structures such as basements and pipelines are not fully covered by flood insurance. While some contents in basements may be covered, the structure itself, including plumbing or electrical systems below ground level, may not be protected.

BASEMENT_CONTENTS.TITLE: Belongings in Basements (Limited Coverage)
BASEMENT_CONTENTS.DESC: Flood insurance provides limited coverage for belongings stored in basements. Items such as furniture and appliances are excluded unless they exceed the required minimum height. Additional coverage may be needed to fully protect the contents of the basement.

WIND_DRIVEN_RAIN.TITLE: Wind-Driven Rain (Without Accompanying Flood)
WIND_DRIVEN_RAIN.DESC: Flood insurance does not cover damage caused by wind-driven rain unless it occurs with a flood. Wind damage is typically covered by homeowners' insurance, but flood policies exclude wind-driven rain unless it's part of a broader flooding event.

PRE_EXISTING_DAMAGE.TITLE: Pre-Existing Flood Damage
PRE_EXISTING_DAMAGE.DESC: Flood insurance does not cover damage from flooding that occurred before the policy's waiting period, typically 30 days. If your property already has flood damage before obtaining flood coverage, the insurance will not cover those damages.

WAITING_PERIOD.TITLE: Losses Occurring Before the Waiting Period Ends (Typically 30 Days)
WAITING_PERIOD.DESC: Flood insurance policies have a waiting period, usually 30 days, before coverage becomes active. Any losses that occur during this waiting period are not covered. Homeowners should plan to purchase insurance before flood risks arise.

NFIP.TITLE: NFIP vs. Private Flood Insurance: Which is Right for You?
NFIP.DESC1: The National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) is a government-backed program that provides flood coverage to homeowners in participating communities. It offers standard coverage limits. NFIP is widely available and often required for federally-backed mortgages in high-risk flood zones. On the other hand, private flood insurance is offered by private insurance companies and can provide higher coverage limits, more flexibility in policy terms, and faster claims processing. It may also cover more types of property and damage than the NFIP.
NFIP.DESC2: When choosing between NFIP and private flood insurance, consider your property’s location, the value of your home, and your coverage needs. If you're in a high-risk flood zone and need affordable, government-backed coverage, NFIP is a solid option. However, if you live in a moderate or low-risk zone and want higher coverage limits or more customized options, private flood insurance might be the better choice. It’s essential to compare premiums, policy options, and exclusions to find the best fit for your needs.

CITY.TITLE: Average Flood Insurance Rates by City in Texas
CITY.DESC: Flood insurance rates in Texas can differ widely from city to city. Urban centers with higher flood risks, older infrastructure, or proximity to rivers and the Gulf Coast often see higher premiums. Meanwhile, inland or lower‑risk areas tend to have more affordable rates. These yearly insurance averages help homeowners compare how location affects their flood insurance costs.

COST.TITLE: How Much Does Flood Insurance Cost in Texas?
COST.DESC1: Flood insurance in Texas varies based on your home's flood risk, location, coverage limits, and whether you choose an NFIP or private policy. On average, Texans pay $779–$879 per year for a standard National Flood Insurance Program policy, which works out to roughly $75 per month. Premiums can be higher in coastal or high‑risk zones and somewhat lower inland. Comparing quotes from both government‑backed and private providers can help you find a competitive price that fits your needs.
COST.DESC2: Compared with other states, Texas flood insurance premiums tend to be near or slightly below the national average. Nationwide, Texans pay a bit less than homeowners in other high‑risk states. However, rates still vary widely based on your exact location and flood zone. Areas prone to frequent flooding or near major water bodies will typically see costs above both the Texas and U.S. averages.

HOW_MUCH_FLOOD.TITLE: How Much Flood Insurance Do You Actually Need?
HOW_MUCH_FLOOD.DESC1: The amount of flood insurance you need depends on the value of your home and personal property, as well as the flood risk in your area. For those with a mortgage in a high-risk flood zone, lenders typically require a minimum coverage amount equal to your loan amount. However, if you're in a low- or moderate-risk area, it's still advisable to consider enough coverage to protect your property from potential flood damage, even if not mandated by your lender.
HOW_MUCH_FLOOD.DESC2: When determining your coverage, consider both building coverage and personal property coverage. Building coverage should cover the full cost of repairing or rebuilding your home, while personal property coverage should cover the value of your belongings. It's important to assess your property's needs carefully and factor in any potential gaps in coverage, especially if you have valuable items or live in an area prone to flooding, even though you're in a lower-risk zone.

HEADER.TITLE: Factors That Impact Your Flood Insurance Rates in Texas
HEADER.DESC: Flood insurance rates in Texas are influenced by several factors, including the flood zone designation, the elevation of your property, and the type of foundation your home has. Other elements, such as the proximity to water bodies, the age of your home, and the level of coverage you choose, also play a role in determining your premiums. Understanding these factors can help you estimate your costs.

FLOOD_ZONE.TITLE: Flood Zone Designation (High-Risk vs. Moderate vs. Low-Risk)
FLOOD_ZONE.DESC: Flood zone designation affects rates, with high-risk areas facing higher premiums than lower-risk zones.

ELEVATION.TITLE: Elevation of Your Property
ELEVATION.DESC: The higher your property's elevation, the lower the flood risk, typically resulting in reduced insurance premiums.

ELEVATION_CERT.TITLE: Elevation Certificate
ELEVATION_CERT.DESC: An elevation certificate can help reduce premiums by providing accurate data about your home's flood risk.

LOCATION.TITLE: Location of Your Property
LOCATION.DESC: Homes closer to water bodies or in coastal regions typically face higher flood insurance premiums due to greater risk.

HOME_AGE.TITLE: Age and Construction of Your Home
HOME_AGE.DESC: Older homes or those with outdated construction typically face higher premiums due to a higher risk of flood damage.

FOUNDATION.TITLE: Type of Foundation (Slab, Crawlspace, Basement)
FOUNDATION.DESC: Homes with basements or crawlspaces generally have higher premiums due to their vulnerability to flooding.

FLOORS.TITLE: Number of Floors in Your Home
FLOORS.DESC: Homes with multiple floors are at greater risk of extensive flood damage, which can lead to higher insurance costs.

FIRST_FLOOR_HEIGHT.TITLE: First Floor Height Above Ground Level
FIRST_FLOOR_HEIGHT.DESC: Homes with a higher first floor face a lower risk of flooding, which generally leads to lower premiums.

WATER_PROXIMITY.TITLE: Proximity to Rivers, Lakes, and Bayous
WATER_PROXIMITY.DESC: Properties near rivers, lakes, or bayous face higher premiums due to the increased risk of flooding from these bodies of water.

GULF_PROXIMITY.TITLE: Proximity to the Gulf Coast
