WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.TITLE: What Is Title Insurance and Why Do You Need It?
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC: Title insurance protects homebuyers and lenders from financial loss due to problems with a property’s ownership history. It ensures the property has a clear legal title before the purchase is finalized.
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC1: Buying a property without title insurance can expose you to hidden claims, unpaid liens, or ownership disputes. It gives peace of mind by protecting your investment from unexpected legal issues.
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.SUB_TITLE: Here are a few reasons why you might need title insurance:

LIST.TITLE: Protection from Ownership Disputes
LIST.TEXT: Title insurance protects you from legal claims or disputes over property ownership that may arise after purchase.

LIST.TITLE: Coverage for Hidden Liens
LIST.TEXT: It safeguards you against unpaid debts, taxes, or liens linked to previous owners of the property.

LIST.TITLE: Ensures Clear Ownership
LIST.TEXT: Title insurance verifies and secures your legal right to fully own the property without unexpected issues.

LIST.TITLE: Financial Protection
LIST.TEXT: It helps cover financial losses caused by title defects or legal challenges related to the property.

LIST.TITLE: Peace of Mind
LIST.TEXT: With title insurance, you can confidently invest in your property knowing your ownership is protected.

HOW_IT_WORKS.TITLE: What Can Go Wrong With a Property Title in Texas?
HOW_IT_WORKS.DESC1: Even after a property purchase, issues can surface in the title history that were not clearly visible during the transaction. In Texas, common problems include unpaid property taxes, contractor liens, recording errors, or missing signatures on past deeds. These issues can call into question who legally owns the property and may create unexpected financial or legal responsibilities for the new owner.
HOW_IT_WORKS.DESC2: More serious complications can arise from disputes over inheritance, unknown heirs claiming ownership, or even fraud in past transfers. Without proper protection, resolving these issues can be costly and time-consuming. That is why many buyers rely on title insurance to help safeguard their ownership rights and avoid unexpected challenges after closing.

STANDARD.TITLE: What Does Title Insurance Cover in Texas?
STANDARD.DESC: Title insurance in Texas protects against financial loss from problems with a property’s title history. It covers issues like unpaid liens, clerical errors in public records, fraud, forgery, and disputes over ownership or inheritance claims. It also helps resolve hidden defects that could affect your legal rights. It ensures peace of mind for buyers and lenders in Texas.

LIST.TITLE: Unknown Liens and Encumbrances on the Property
LIST.DESC: Title insurance protects from unknown liens or financial claims attached to the property from previous owners, including unpaid debts, contractor fees, or legal judgments that were not disclosed during purchase and could affect ownership rights.

LIST.TITLE: Forged or Fraudulent Deeds and Signatures
LIST.DESC: Coverage protects against losses arising from forged or fraudulent signatures on property deeds or transfer documents. If someone illegally transfers ownership without proper authority, title insurance helps defend your ownership financial interest.

LIST.TITLE: Errors and Omissions in Public Records
LIST.DESC: Mistakes in public records, such as misspelled names, incorrect property descriptions, or filing errors, impact ownership rights. Title insurance covers losses and legal disputes resulting from these administrative or recording inaccuracies in documents.

LIST.TITLE: Undisclosed or Missing Heirs Claiming Ownership
LIST.DESC: If unknown heirs of previous owners claim rights to the property after purchase, title insurance helps protect you. It covers legal defense costs and potential losses arising from inheritance disputes or unexpected ownership challenges.

LIST.TITLE: Boundary and Survey Disputes
LIST.DESC: Disputes over property boundaries or incorrect survey details can lead to conflicts with neighbors or loss of land. Title insurance helps cover legal costs and losses arising from inaccurate surveys or overlapping property lines affecting ownership.

LIST.TITLE: Unpaid Property Taxes From Previous Owners
LIST.DESC: If previous owners failed to pay property taxes, those debts may transfer to you after purchase. Title insurance protects against financial responsibility for unpaid taxes, ensuring you are not held liable for past obligations linked to the property.

LIST.TITLE: Illegal Deeds Signed Under Duress or Incapacity
LIST.DESC: Title insurance covers situations in which prior property transfers were made under pressure, through fraud, or due to mental incapacity. If a deed is later declared invalid, it protects ownership rights and helps cover related legal defense and financial losses.

LIST.TITLE: Easements and Access Rights Not Disclosed at Closing
LIST.DESC: Undisclosed easements or access rights may allow others to use parts of your property, limiting control or value. Title insurance helps protect against financial loss and legal issues arising from undisclosed agreements that affect property use.

LIST.TITLE: Title Defects That Existed Before Your Purchase
LIST.DESC: Pre-existing title defects such as unresolved claims, incorrect ownership history, or missing documentation can surface after purchase. Title insurance protects you from financial loss and legal disputes linked to issues that existed before ownership transfer.

LIST.TITLE: Legal Defense Costs if Your Title Is Challenged
LIST.DESC: If someone challenges your ownership rights, title insurance covers legal defense costs and potential financial losses. It protects you against costly litigation and helps secure your rightful ownership of the property.

TYPES.TITLE: Types of Title Insurance Policies in Texas

LIST.TITLE: Owner's Title Insurance Policy
LIST.DESC: An owner's title insurance policy protects the buyer’s ownership rights from title defects, liens, or disputes existing before the purchase is completed.

LIST.TITLE: Lender's Title Insurance Policy (Loan Policy)
LIST.DESC: Lender's title insurance policy (loan policy) protects the mortgage lender’s interest only if title issues or ownership disputes arise after closing.

LIST.TITLE: Enhanced Owner's Title Insurance Policy
LIST.DESC: Enhanced owner's title insurance policy offers expanded coverage, protecting against additional risks like zoning issues and certain hidden defects.

LIST.TITLE: Leasehold Title Insurance Policy
LIST.DESC: Leasehold title insurance policy protects tenants or leaseholders, covering title issues affecting long-term leased property rights and agreements.

LIST.TITLE: Construction Loan Title Insurance Policy
LIST.DESC: A construction loan title insurance policy protects lenders during property construction, covering title defects or claims that arise only while building.

LIST.TITLE: Refinance Title Insurance Policy
LIST.DESC: Refinance title insurance protects homeowners when refinancing, ensuring the new loan has a clear title and no hidden legal issues in the coverage.

LIST.TITLE: Commercial Title Insurance Policy
LIST.DESC: Commercial title insurance policy protects business properties, ensuring ownership clarity and covering risks tied to commercial real estate deals.

LIST.TITLE: Vacant Land Title Insurance Policy
LIST.DESC: Vacant land title insurance policy protects buyers purchasing undeveloped land, covering title issues that may affect future property development.

LIST.TITLE: Simultaneous Issue Title Insurance Policy
LIST.DESC: Simultaneous issue title insurance policy is issued with lender and owner policies together, reducing cost and ensuring both parties are protected.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Title Insurance NOT Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Title insurance in Texas does not cover issues that arise after the policy is issued, such as new liens, zoning violations, or environmental hazards. It also excludes property condition problems, structural defects, or maintenance issues. Additionally, it does not protect against government actions, fraud occurring after purchase, or disputes not related to the title history.

POOR_WORKMANSHIP.TITLE: Title Defects Created After the Policy Issue Date
POOR_WORKMANSHIP.DESC: Title insurance does not cover defects or issues that arise after the policy is issued. Any new claims, ownership changes, or legal problems occurring post-purchase are excluded, leaving the buyer responsible for protecting future risks and changes.

NON_PAYMENT_SUBS.TITLE: Zoning Violations and Land Use Restrictions
NON_PAYMENT_SUBS.DESC: Title insurance does not protect against zoning violations or land use restrictions imposed by local authorities. If a property is used in ways that violate zoning laws or future restrictions arise, those issues are excluded from coverage entirely.

WORKER_INJURY.TITLE: Environmental Hazards and Contamination
WORKER_INJURY.DESC: Environmental hazards such as soil contamination, hazardous waste, or pollution are not covered by title insurance. Any cleanup costs or health risks associated with environmental conditions remain the property owner's responsibility under the law.

THIRD_PARTY_DAMAGE.TITLE: Physical Damage to the Property
THIRD_PARTY_DAMAGE.DESC: Title insurance does not cover physical damage to the property, such as fire, flood, storms, or structural deterioration. These risks fall under homeowners' insurance, not title protection, leaving maintenance and repairs covered entirely under the owner's policy.

EQUIPMENT_THEFT.TITLE: Homeowner Association (HOA) Disputes and Violations
EQUIPMENT_THEFT.DESC: Title insurance does not cover Homeowner Association disputes, fees, or rule violations. Any penalties, assessments, or conflicts with HOA regulations must be handled directly by the property owner, without insurance coverage.

DESIGN_ERRORS.TITLE: Unpermitted Construction or Building Code Violations
DESIGN_ERRORS.DESC: Title insurance does not cover unpermitted construction or building code violations on the property. Any fines, corrections, or compliance costs required by local authorities must be handled by the owner without insurance coverage.

FORCE_MAJEURE.TITLE: Eminent Domain and Government Takings
FORCE_MAJEURE.DESC: Title insurance does not protect against eminent domain or government takings of private property for public use. Any compensation or legal process is handled by government authorities and is not covered directly under the title insurance policy.

CHANGE_ORDERS.TITLE: Defects Known to the Buyer Before Closing
CHANGE_ORDERS.DESC: Title insurance does not cover defects that the buyer already knew about before closing the purchase. Any pre-disclosed issues or agreed conditions are excluded from protection under the insurance policy terms and agreements that are fully in place.

CONTRACTOR_INSOLVENCY.TITLE: Mechanic's Liens Filed After the Policy Date
CONTRACTOR_INSOLVENCY.DESC: Title insurance does not cover mechanics’ liens or claims filed after the policy's effective date. Any work-related debts or contractor claims arising after issuance are excluded from protection under the policy but are fully included.

ENVIRONMENTAL.TITLE: Losses Caused by the Policyholder's Own Actions
ENVIRONMENTAL.DESC: Title insurance does not cover losses caused by the policyholder’s own actions, negligence, or illegal activity. Any damage, fraud, or violations committed by the owner are excluded from coverage under the insurance policy terms and conditions.

HEALTH_INSURANCE_COST.TITLE: How Much Does Title Insurance Cost in Texas?
HEALTH_INSURANCE_COST.DESC1: Title insurance cost in Texas is regulated by the Texas Department of Insurance, meaning every licensed provider follows the same base premium schedule. According to Neuhaus Realty Group, a standard owner’s title insurance policy in Texas typically ranges from $832 to $4,162 for a $485,000 home, depending on the property's value and the rate tier applied.
HEALTH_INSURANCE_COST.DESC2: Compared with other states, Texas pricing is more structured because rates are government-regulated, so there is no price shopping among companies. Nationally, title insurance generally costs around 0.5% to 1% of the home’s purchase price, which can translate to roughly $2,000–$4,000 on a $400,000 home, depending on state rules and risk factors. In many states, prices vary by insurer, but in Texas, costs remain consistent and predictable across providers.

HEADER.DESC: Title insurance protects buyers from past ownership issues like liens, fraud, or disputes, ensuring clear property rights. WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.TITLE: What Is a Title Transfer and Why Does It Matter?
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC: A title transfer is the formal legal procedure that updates ownership records to reflect a new owner. This involves submitting the required documents, verifying the transfer's legitimacy, and recording the change with the relevant authority (such as the county clerk for property transfers or the DMV for vehicle transfers).
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC1: Without a proper title transfer, you may face ownership disputes, fines, or difficulty selling the asset later. It is the only way to ensure your legal right to property or a vehicle is recognized.
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.SUB_TITLE: Here’s why title transfer matters:

LIST.TITLE: Establishes Legal Ownership
LIST.TEXT: A title transfer legally proves who owns the property or asset. Without it, disputes can arise over who has the rightful claim.

LIST.TITLE: Protects Buyers and Sellers
LIST.TEXT: It protects both parties in a transaction. Buyers gain confirmed ownership, and sellers are released from future liability.

LIST.TITLE: Prevents Legal Disputes
LIST.TEXT: Proper documentation reduces the risk of family disputes, fraud, or third-party claims over the same property or asset.

LIST.TITLE: Required by Law for Most Transfers
LIST.TEXT: Ownership changes—whether real estate or vehicles—must be officially recorded to be valid and recognized by government authorities.

LIST.TITLE: Ensures Smooth Future Transactions
LIST.TEXT: A properly transferred title makes it easier to sell, refinance, or transfer the property again in the future without delays or legal complications.

WHEN_DO_YOU_NEED.TITLE: When Do You Need a Title Transfer in Texas?
WHEN_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC: You need a title transfer in Texas whenever ownership of a property or asset legally changes hands. This commonly happens when buying or selling real estate, purchasing or selling a vehicle, receiving property as a gift, or inheriting assets through probate or an affidavit of heirship. It is also required in situations like divorce settlements, adding or removing a co-owner, or transferring property into a trust or business entity. In each of these cases, the title must be updated so the new ownership is officially recorded with the appropriate Texas authority.
WHEN_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC1: A title transfer in Texas is especially important any time there is a change in legal responsibility or financial interest tied to the asset. Even if the agreement between parties is informal or within family members, the transfer still needs to be documented to avoid future disputes, tax issues, or ownership conflicts. Without completing this process, the previous owner may still be held liable, and the new owner may not have full legal rights to the property or vehicle.

HOW_IT_WORKS.TITLE: How Does the Title Transfer Process Work in Texas?
HOW_IT_WORKS.DESC1: The title transfer process in Texas begins by gathering the required documents for the type of transfer, such as a deed for real estate or a title certificate for a vehicle. Both parties usually need to complete and sign the appropriate forms, provide valid identification, and ensure any existing liens or loans on the property are properly addressed. In real estate cases, a title search is often conducted to confirm clear ownership before the transfer can proceed. For vehicles, the odometer disclosure and bill of sale may also be required depending on the situation.
HOW_IT_WORKS.DESC2: Once the paperwork is ready, it must be submitted to the correct authority—typically the county clerk’s office for property or the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles for vehicles. Recording fees and applicable taxes are paid at this stage, and the documents are officially processed. After approval, the ownership records are updated to reflect the new owner. This completes the title transfer process in Texas, making the change of ownership legally valid and recognized by the state.

TYPES.TITLE: Types of Title Transfers in Texas

LIST.TITLE: Real Estate Title Transfer (Sale or Purchase)
LIST.DESC: Used when ownership of property changes through buying or selling, ensuring legal record updates with county authorities for legality.

LIST.TITLE: Vehicle Title Transfer
LIST.DESC: Required when ownership of a vehicle changes hands, updating official records to reflect the new registered owner correctly.

LIST.TITLE: Gift Title Transfer
LIST.DESC: Used when property or assets are given without payment, requiring legal documentation to record new ownership with the authorities.

LIST.TITLE: Inheritance Title Transfer (Probate or Affidavit of Heirship)
LIST.DESC: Used to pass ownership after death through legal heirs, ensuring property is recorded under the rightful successors officially.

LIST.TITLE: Quitclaim Deed Title Transfer
LIST.DESC: Transfers whatever interest a person has in property without guarantees, often used for quick or family-based changes.

LIST.TITLE: Divorce Settlement Title Transfer
LIST.DESC: Used when property is divided between spouses after divorce, updating ownership records according to the settlement agreement legally.

LIST.TITLE: Trust Title Transfer
LIST.DESC: Moves ownership of property into or out of a trust for estate planning and asset protection purposes under the legal structure of TX.

LIST.TITLE: Business Entity Title Transfer
LIST.DESC: Transfers ownership interests when a company changes structure or ownership, ensuring proper legal registration updates and compliance.

LIST.TITLE: Tax Deed Title Transfer
LIST.DESC: Occurs when property is transferred after a tax sale for unpaid taxes, thereby changing legal ownership to the buyer through the court process.

HEALTH_INSURANCE_COST.TITLE: How Much Does a Title Transfer Cost in Texas?
HEALTH_INSURANCE_COST.DESC1: The cost of a title transfer in Texas typically starts with a base title application fee of about $28 to $33, depending on the county where the transaction is processed. In addition, most transfers include a $4.75 state processing fee, and for vehicle-related transfers, a 6.25% motor vehicle sales tax is applied based on the purchase price or the standard vehicle value. Some situations may also include small county or registration-related charges, making the total cost vary depending on the type and complexity of the transfer.

WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.TITLE: What Is Pet Insurance and Why Do You Need It?
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.DESC: Pet insurance is a type of financial protection that helps cover the cost of veterinary care when your dog or cat gets sick, injured, or needs medical treatment. Instead of paying the full vet bill out of pocket, you pay a monthly premium and the insurance company reimburses a portion of eligible expenses based on your plan. In simple terms, it works like health insurance for your pet—helping you manage unexpected and often expensive vet costs so you can focus on your pet’s recovery instead of financial stress.
WHY_DO_YOU_NEED.SUB_TITLE: Here’s why you need pet insurance:

LIST.TITLE: Protects You From High Vet Bills
LIST.TEXT: Emergency surgeries, hospital stays, or accident treatments can cost hundreds or even thousands of dollars. Insurance helps reduce this burden.

LIST.TITLE: Ensures Faster Medical Decisions
LIST.TEXT: When finances are not a barrier, you can approve treatments quickly, which can be critical in emergencies.

LIST.TITLE: Covers Unexpected Illnesses and Accidents
LIST.TEXT: From infections to broken bones, pets can get sick or injured without warning, and treatment costs can add up fast.

LIST.TITLE: Supports Long-Term Health Care
LIST.TEXT: Chronic conditions like diabetes or arthritis often require ongoing treatment, medications, and follow-ups.

LIST.TITLE: Gives Peace of Mind for Pet Owners
LIST.TEXT: Knowing you’re financially prepared allows you to focus on your pet’s care rather than worrying about unexpected expenses.

HOW_IT_WORKS.TITLE: How Much Do Unexpected Vet Bills Cost in Texas Without Pet Insurance?
HOW_IT_WORKS.DESC1: Without pet insurance in Texas, vet bills can add up quickly, especially when care is unexpected. A simple wellness visit may cost $50-$150, but once tests, medications, or additional services are added, the total can easily rise to $200–$500 per visit. Emergency clinic visits are even more costly, often starting with a $100–$200 exam fee alone, before any treatment is done.
HOW_IT_WORKS.DESC2: For serious emergencies or surgeries, costs can escalate into the hundreds or even thousands of dollars. In Texas, emergency treatment and hospitalization typically range from $500 to $5,000, depending on severity, diagnostic tests, and length of stay. Procedures like surgery, X-rays, or intensive care can quickly push the bill even higher, making unexpected vet emergencies a major financial burden for pet owners without coverage.

STANDARD.TITLE: What Does Pet Insurance Cover in Texas?
STANDARD.DESC: Pet insurance in Texas helps cover a wide range of veterinary expenses that can arise from unexpected accidents or illnesses. Most plans reimburse costs for emergency care, surgeries, hospitalization, diagnostic tests, prescription medications, and chronic conditions. Depending on the plan, coverage may also include cancer treatment, specialist care, and preventive wellness services.

LIST.TITLE: Accidents and Emergency Veterinary Care
LIST.DESC: Helps pay for sudden injuries like fractures, bites, poisoning, or trauma from accidents. It further includes ER visits, urgent treatment, and stabilization, ensuring your pets receive the immediate medical attention they need.

LIST.TITLE: Illnesses and Chronic Conditions
LIST.DESC: Covers illnesses and chronic conditions, including infections, allergies, diabetes, arthritis, and long-term diseases. Helps pay for diagnostics, medications, and ongoing treatments that manage your pet's health over time and improve quality of life.

LIST.TITLE: Surgery and Hospitalization
LIST.DESC: Surgery and hospitalization coverage helps pay for both routine and emergency operations, including pre-operative care, surgical procedures, anesthesia, and post-operative recovery. It also covers overnight hospital stays and intensive monitoring.

LIST.TITLE: Prescription Medications
LIST.DESC: Cover prescription medications prescribed by a vet to treat injuries, infections, or chronic illnesses. This includes antibiotics, pain-relief drugs, allergy treatments, and long-term medications for ongoing health conditions and recovery support.

LIST.TITLE: Diagnostic Tests, X-Rays, and Lab Work
LIST.DESC: Coverage includes diagnostic tests such as blood work, urine tests, X-rays, and advanced lab tests used to detect health issues. These tests help vets identify problems early and create accurate treatment plans for recovery and long-term management.

LIST.TITLE: Cancer Treatment and Chemotherapy
LIST.DESC: Pays for expensive cancer treatments, including chemotherapy, radiation therapy, medications, and supportive care. It reduces the financial burden of long-term cancer management while ensuring pets receive proper and timely medical attention.

LIST.TITLE: Specialist and Referral Care
LIST.DESC: This coverage helps pay for visits to veterinary specialists, including cardiologists, neurologists, dermatologists, and orthopedic specialists. It is used when pets need advanced diagnosis or treatment beyond general veterinary care for complex conditions.

LIST.TITLE: Hereditary and Congenital Conditions (on select plans)
LIST.DESC: Some plans cover hereditary and congenital conditions that are genetic or present at birth. This includes breed-specific health issues that may require ongoing treatment, testing, or management depending on the policy and level of coverage selected.

LIST.TITLE: Preventive and Wellness Care (on comprehensive plans)
LIST.DESC: Includes routine care like vaccinations, annual checkups, flea and tick prevention, dental cleanings, and screenings. It helps maintain overall pet health and prevents serious illnesses through early detection and veterinary care.

LIST.TITLE: Dental Illness and Tooth Extractions (on select plans)
LIST.DESC: Some plans cover dental diseases such as infections, gum disease, and tooth decay. It may also include tooth extractions and related treatments needed to relieve pain, prevent complications, and maintain good oral health in pets over time.

TYPES.TITLE: Types of Pet Insurance Plans in Texas

LIST.TITLE: Accident-Only Pet Insurance
LIST.DESC: Covers injuries from accidents like fractures, burns, or poisoning. It's a basic, budget-friendly plan for emergency situations only.

LIST.TITLE: Accident and Illness Pet Insurance
LIST.DESC: Covers both accidents and illnesses, including infections, surgeries, and chronic diseases. It offers broader protection than basic plans.

LIST.TITLE: Comprehensive Pet Insurance (Accident, Illness, and Wellness)
LIST.DESC: Includes accident, illness, and routine wellness care, such as vaccines and checkups, offering the most complete protection for pets.

LIST.TITLE: Wellness and Preventive Care Plans
LIST.DESC: Focuses on routine care, including vaccinations, exams, dental cleanings, and parasite prevention, to maintain overall pet health.

LIST.TITLE: Lifetime Pet Insurance Plans
LIST.DESC: Provides ongoing coverage for chronic conditions throughout your pet's life, as long as the policy remains active and premiums are paid.

LIST.TITLE: Time-Limited Pet Insurance Plans
LIST.DESC: Covers specific illnesses or injuries for a set period, usually up to 12 months, after which coverage for that condition ends.

LIST.TITLE: Per-Condition Pet Insurance Plans
LIST.DESC: Sets a financial limit for each condition, covering treatment costs until the limit is reached for that specific illness or injury.

LIST.TITLE: Multi-Pet Insurance Plans
LIST.DESC: Allows coverage for multiple pets under a single policy, often offering discounts and easier insurance management for households.

HEADER.TITLE: What Does Pet Insurance NOT Cover in Texas?
HEADER.DESC: Pet insurance in Texas helps with many veterinary costs, but it does not cover everything. Most policies exclude pre-existing conditions, cosmetic or elective procedures, and routine grooming. Certain preventive treatments, breeding-related expenses, and experimental therapies are not included. Understanding exclusions helps pet owners choose the right plan and avoid surprises when filing claims.

PRE_EXISTING.TITLE: Pre-Existing Conditions
PRE_EXISTING.DESC: Pre-existing conditions are illnesses or injuries your pet had before the insurance policy started. These are usually not covered because they are considered ongoing or prior health issues, even if symptoms reappear later during the policy period.

ROUTINE_CARE.TITLE: Routine and Preventive Care (on basic plans)
ROUTINE_CARE.DESC: Basic pet insurance plans typically do not cover routine and preventive care, such as vaccinations, annual checkups, or wellness exams. These services are considered standard maintenance and are only included in comprehensive or wellness add-on plans.

COSMETIC.TITLE: Cosmetic Procedures and Elective Surgery
COSMETIC.DESC: Such procedures are not covered because they are not medically necessary. This includes tail docking, ear cropping, or other surgeries performed for appearance rather than to treat an illness, injury, or health-related condition in pets.

BREEDING.TITLE: Breeding, Pregnancy, and Whelping Costs
BREEDING.DESC: Costs related to breeding, pregnancy care, and delivery are usually excluded. This includes prenatal checkups, complications during birth, and care for newborn puppies or kittens unless specifically added in a special breeding-related policy.

GROOMING.TITLE: Grooming and Bathing
GROOMING.DESC: Routine grooming and bathing are not covered since they are part of regular pet maintenance. This includes haircuts, nail trimming, and hygiene grooming services that are not related to any medical treatment or diagnosed skin condition.

PARASITES.TITLE: Parasites and Flea Prevention (on most plans)
PARASITES.DESC: Most standard plans do not cover parasite prevention, such as flea, tick, or worm treatments. These are considered routine preventive care and are usually only included in wellness add-on packages or separate preventive coverage options.

EXPERIMENTAL.TITLE: Experimental or Investigational Treatments
EXPERIMENTAL.DESC: These treatments are not covered because they are not widely approved or proven. This includes new therapies, untested medications, or procedures that are still in clinical trials and lack established veterinary effectiveness or safety data.

BEHAVIORAL.TITLE: Behavioral Training and Therapy (on most plans)
BEHAVIORAL.DESC: Training and therapy for issues like aggression or anxiety are usually excluded. These services are considered non-medical unless linked to a covered medical condition and included in a specialized or upgraded insurance plan.

DENTAL_CLEANING.TITLE: Dental Cleaning and Routine Oral Care
DENTAL_CLEANING.DESC: Routine dental cleanings and general oral care are not covered in basic plans. These preventive services are considered maintenance care unless a dental illness or emergency condition requires treatment under a higher-level policy.

NEGLECT.TITLE: Injuries Caused by Neglect or Abuse
NEGLECT.DESC: Injuries resulting from neglect or abuse are not covered by pet insurance. Policies exclude these cases because they are preventable and violate standard care responsibilities expected from pet owners under insurance terms and conditions.

HEALTH_INSURANCE_COST.TITLE: How Much Does Pet Insurance Cost in Texas?
HEALTH_INSURANCE_COST.DESC1: Pet insurance in Texas typically costs around $56 per month for dogs and $24 per month for cats, depending on breed, age, coverage level, and deductible choices. On average, pet owners pay about $49 per month for standard accident and illness coverage, while comprehensive plans with wellness benefits can cost more.

HEADER.DESC: Insurance rates for cat breeds in Texas differ primarily because insurers assess genetic health risks, hereditary diseases, and medical histories associated with each breed. As pets move from young to senior stages, insurers adjust premiums to reflect higher claim risks and rising treatment costs. Younger pets are cheaper because they are healthier and less likely to need expensive procedures.

ITEMS.LIABILITY: Liability coverage pays for injuries and property damage you cause to others in an accident. It covers medical bills, repairs, and legal costs, so you do not pay everything yourself later.
ITEMS.COLLISION: Collision coverage helps pay to repair or replace your car if it is damaged in an accident, no matter who is at fault. It applies after crashes with cars or other objects to help protect you.
ITEMS.COMPREHENSIVE: Comprehensive coverage protects your car from theft, vandalism, fire, storms, flooding, or falling objects. It covers non-accident damage, giving broader protection for your vehicle.
ITEMS.PIP: PIP covers medical bills, lost wages, and rehab costs after an accident, regardless of fault. It provides fast financial support and helps you recover easily after a crash without stress.
ITEMS.MEDPAY: MedPay helps pay medical expenses for you and passengers after an accident, regardless of fault. It covers hospital visits and treatment quickly, so care is not delayed or stressful.
ITEMS.UM: UM coverage protects you if hit by a driver without insurance. It covers medical bills and damages when the at-fault driver cannot cover the costs, keeping you financially safe at all times.
ITEMS.UIM: UIM helps when the at-fault driver has insurance but not enough to cover your full medical or repair costs after a serious accident, giving you extra financial protection when needed.
ITEMS.UMPD: UMPD covers repair costs if your car is damaged by an uninsured driver. It ensures you do not pay out of pocket after a crash, protecting your vehicle from unexpected expenses.
ITEMS.ROADSIDE: Roadside assistance helps when your car breaks down, offering towing, tire changes, jump-starts, lockout assistance, and fuel delivery so you are never stranded during your emergencies.
ITEMS.RENTAL: Rental reimbursement covers a rental car while your vehicle is being repaired after a covered accident, helping you stay mobile at no extra cost when your car is in the shop.
ITEMS.GAP: Gap insurance covers the difference between your car loan and the actual value if the vehicle is totaled or stolen, helping you avoid paying the remaining loan balance out of pocket.
ITEMS.TOWING: Towing and labor coverage pays for towing and minor roadside repairs when your car breaks down unexpectedly, helping you get back on the road quickly without high out-of-pocket costs.
ITEMS.CUSTOM_PARTS: Custom parts coverage protects upgrades like rims, sound systems, or modifications if your car is damaged or stolen, ensuring your added investments stay financially protected.
ITEMS.RIDESHARE: Rideshare coverage protects drivers working for Uber or Lyft, filling gaps when personal insurance does not apply while driving for hire, ensuring safer coverage while earning income.
ITEMS.LOAN_PAYOFF: Loan payoff coverage helps pay off your remaining loan if your car is totaled and worth less than what you owe, protecting you from paying a balance after losing your vehicle unexpectedly.
ITEMS.NEW_CAR: New car replacement provides a brand-new vehicle of the same model if your new car is totaled during a covered period, helping you quickly recover full value after a major loss.
ITEMS.ACCIDENT_FORGIVENESS: Accident forgiveness prevents your insurance rates from increasing after your first at-fault accident, helping keep premiums stable over time, giving you financial protection and peace.
ITEMS.DEATH_DISABILITY: Death and disability coverage provides financial support if you are seriously injured or killed in an accident, helping protect your family's financial future during difficult times.

ITEMS.LIABILITY: Covers medical expenses and property damage you cause to others in an accident. It pays for injuries to others and repairs to their property, but does not cover your own car or medical costs.
ITEMS.COLLISION: Pays to repair or replace your own vehicle after a collision, regardless of who caused the accident. After you pay your deductible, it helps cover damage from crashes with other objects, such as fences.
ITEMS.COMPREHENSIVE: Helps pay for damage to your vehicle caused by events other than a collision. This includes coverage of theft, vandalism, hailstorms, flooding, fire, falling objects, and even animal strikes.
ITEMS.PIP: Helps cover medical expenses for you and passengers after an accident, regardless of fault. It can also help with lost wages and essential services, such as childcare, if injuries prevent you from working.
ITEMS.MEDPAY: Pays for medical treatment after a car accident for you and your passengers, regardless of who caused the crash. It covers hospital visits, ambulance fees, and other medical costs up to the policy limit.
ITEMS.UM: Protects you if you are hit by a driver who has no insurance. It pays for your medical bills, lost income, and sometimes vehicle repairs. This is important in areas with high rates of uninsured drivers.
ITEMS.UIM: Helps cover costs when the at-fault driver has insurance, but not enough to fully pay for your medical bills or vehicle repairs. It fills the gap between their limited coverage and your actual expenses.
ITEMS.UMPD: Pays for damage to your vehicle caused by an uninsured driver when they are responsible for the accident. This ensures you are not left paying for repairs when the other driver cannot cover the costs.
ITEMS.ROADSIDE: Provides help when your vehicle breaks down on the road. Services may include towing, jump-starts, flat tire changes, fuel delivery, and lockout assistance. It offers quick support during emergencies so you are not stranded far from help.
ITEMS.RENTAL: Helps pay for a rental car while your vehicle is being repaired after a covered accident. This ensures you can continue your daily activities, like commuting or running errands, while your car is in the shop for repairs.
ITEMS.GAP: Covers the difference between what you owe on your auto loan or lease and your vehicle's actual cash value if totaled. This prevents paying out of pocket for a car you no longer drive, but still owe.
ITEMS.TOWING: Pays for towing and basic roadside labor when your vehicle breaks down unexpectedly. It helps cover costs such as towing to a repair shop, providing financial relief during unexpected vehicle issues.
ITEMS.CUSTOM_PARTS: Covers aftermarket additions or upgrades made to your vehicle, such as custom rims, sound systems, or performance parts. These modifications are often not included in standard insurance policies.
ITEMS.RIDESHARE: Provides protection while driving for rideshare services like Uber or Lyft. It fills gaps between personal auto insurance and the commercial policy provided by the rideshare company, ensuring protection.
ITEMS.LOAN_PAYOFF: Pays off the remaining balance on your auto loan or lease if your vehicle is totaled and its value is less than what you owe. This protects from continuing payments on a car that is no longer usable.
ITEMS.NEW_CAR: Provides a replacement vehicle of the same make and model if your new car is totaled within a certain time period or mileage limit. It avoids depreciation losses early in ownership and keeps you driving.
ITEMS.ACCIDENT_FORGIVENESS: Protects your insurance rates from increasing after your first at-fault accident. It ensures that a single mistake does not affect your premium, helping to maintain more stable insurance costs over time.
ITEMS.DEATH_DISABILITY: Provides support to you or your family if you suffer serious injury, disability, or death in a covered accident. It helps replace lost income and cover expenses during difficult times following a crash.
